title: Overview of Government's Strategy to Emerge Stronger from the COVID-19 Pandemic
what_it_is: Overview of Government's Strategy to Emerge Stronger from the COVID-19 Pandemic

sections.label: Pandemic support package funding
sections.summary: The Government committed $100 billion for pandemic support, using past surpluses and $52 billion from reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Since February this year, the Government has committed a massive $100 billion to help businesses and Singaporeans cope with the pandemic fallout.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: To fund this gigantic support package, we have used up all of the accumulated surpluses from the last term of Government and also drawn on reserves for an unprecedented amount of $52 billion.

sections.label: Cost of continuing support measures
sections.summary: Continuing the support measures would cost the Government a further $8 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The continuation of these support measures would cost the Government a further $8 billion.

sections.label: Projected record overall deficit
sections.summary: Even with the NIRC added, the Government is likely to run a record overall deficit of $74.2 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Even with the NIRC added, the Government is likely to run an overall deficit of $ 74.2 billion; a record number in our history.

sections.label: Question on further reserves draw
sections.summary: It asks whether the Government would consider another draw on reserves given the crisis magnitude and investment items.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider a further draw on the reserves again; considering the magnitude and severity of this crisis and these are essentially also investment items?

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centre
sections.summary: The SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centre in the heartlands has drawn hundreds seeking jobs and training since August.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: One notable commitment by the Government is the setting up of the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centre at the heartlands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Since the opening in August, hundreds of residents have sought jobs and training opportunities at the centre and I have received emails of gratitude from residents who have found employment through the centre.

sections.label: Support for SGUnited centres
sections.summary: The SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centre is commended, and the Manpower Minister is asked to keep resourcing it beyond the crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The friendly job counsellor were always there to reassure you, to help point out to the opportunities out there and these are all important psychological support as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: So, the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centre is a commendable initiative by MOM and I appeal to the Manpower Minister to continue supporting and resourcing the centres well beyond the crisis.

sections.label: Quality investments drawn in
sections.summary: MTI and EDB continued to draw in quality investments in recent months, including the Hyundai Motor Group Innovation Centre, Siemens Advance Manufacturing Competence Centre and Tata Consultancy's Digital Acceleration Centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: MTI and EDB continued to draw in quality investments in recent months like the new Hyundai Motor Group Innovation Centre, Siemens Advance Manufacturing Competence Centre, Tata Consultancy’s Digital Acceleration Centre and others.

sections.label: Diversified economic structure resilience
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister mentioned that resilience was achieved through a diversified economic structure where no one industry accounts for more than 20% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Deputy Prime Minister also mentioned how we achieved resilience through a diversified economic structure, where no one industry accounts for more than 20% of our GDP.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme employee subsidies
sections.summary: Each employee is supported by up to around $50,000 worth of subsidies over a 17-month period if their companies are eligible for the highest tier of the Jobs Support Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Each employee is supported by up to around $50,000 worth of subsidies over a 17-month period if their companies are eligible for the highest tier of the Jobs Support Scheme or JSS.

sections.label: CPF early access proposal
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to consider letting CPF members temporarily tap a small amount of their CPF for emergencies, citing Australia's early superannuation release.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: On that basis, if overall average household financial conditions do worsen, I urge the Government to consider allowing CPF members to temporarily tap on a small amount of their CPF to resolve their emergencies if needed, subject to eligibility criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In Australia, for example, in July this year, as part of the jobseeker policy measures, those affected by COVID-19 are allowed early release access up to AUD10,000 of their superannuation in fiscal year 2019/20 and a further AUD10,000 in fiscal year 2020/21.

sections.label: Loan deferment data and task force
sections.summary: The Government shared loan deferment data, and the speaker suggests an inter-agency post-COVID-19 financial conditions task force to address a potential debt cliff effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Government had previously shared some data on loan deferments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We are looking at 38,900 applications for property loan repayment deferments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Out of these, 90% or $20 billion worth of mortgage deferments were approved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It would be good to know what proportion is owed to banks versus those to HDB loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Which SME sectors are affected most by the moratorium?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I worry about a potential "household and corporate debt" cliff effect when the extension of payment moratorium ends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One way is to form an inter-agency post-COVID-19 financial conditions task force to ensure as much help is provided as we wean away from some of the payment moratoriums when it happens.

sections.label: Baby Support Grant eligibility extension
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will consider extending the $3,000 Baby Support Grant eligibility to include babies born in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: My last point is on the $3,000 Baby Support Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic and even before the circuit breaker, many people were laid off or had their work hours and salaries cut.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I hope the Government will consider extending eligibility to include babies born in 2020.

sections.label: MAS Budgets GDP estimate
sections.summary: MAS estimates the combined Budgets will prevent the economy from contracting by a further 5.6% of GDP in 2020 and 4.8% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The MAS estimates that the combined Budgets will prevent the economy from contracting by a further 5.6% of GDP in 2020 and 4.8% in 2021.

sections.label: SME share of JSS
sections.summary: SMEs get $10.5 billion of the $16 billion given to firms, about 65% of JSS, while SME workers are 73% of local workers supported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As Deputy Prime Minister Heng has clarified, SMEs currently get $10.5 billion out of the $16 billion that has been given out to firms thus far.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That accounts for about 65% of the total amount of JSS being given out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, SME workers consist of 73% of the local workers supported by JSS.

sections.label: Australian turnover and income tests
sections.summary: Businesses with AUD1 billion or less turnover need a 30% income fall, while those above need a 50% or more fall to qualify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For their scheme, businesses with AUD1 billion or less in aggregated turnover require a fall in expected or realised income by 30%, whereas businesses with an aggregated turnover of more than AUD1 billion will require an expected or realised fall in income by 50% or more to qualify for the same scheme.

sections.label: NIRC and reserves clarification
sections.summary: NIRC estimates as at 18 February and revised FY2020 estimates are the same at $18.63 billion, and reserves drawn equal over 20 years of past Budget surpluses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Thirdly, I would like to seek clarification regarding the expected NIRC contribution in the revised revenue estimates and FY2020 fiscal position under the Third Supplementary Estimates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In it, I note that the NIRC estimates as at 18 February and the revised FY2020 estimates today are the same at $18.63 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In MOF's Addendum to the President's Address in August this year, I note that we have drawn on our reserves equivalent to over 20 years of past Budget surpluses.

sections.label: Development expenditure reductions by Ministries
sections.summary: Development expenditures across Ministries are lowered by $6.8 billion, including MOT at $3.59 billion, MTI at $744 million and MND at $614 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Development expenditures across Ministries are lowered by a substantial $6.8 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Among the notable reductions are MOT at $3.59 billion, MTI at $744 million and MND at $614 million.

sections.label: Redundancies in first half 2020
sections.summary: MOM's latest labour market report shows more than 11,000 jobs made redundant in the first half of 2020, excluding recent large-scale layoffs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to the latest labour market report published by MOM, more than 11,000 jobs were made redundant in the first half of 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: This figure does not include the large-scale layoffs recently announced by Resorts World Sentosa and Singapore Airlines, and we can expect that retrenchment and unemployment numbers will continue to rise in the second half of the year.

sections.label: Right to Disconnect legislation
sections.summary: The speaker asked in the House whether it was timely to consider a Right to Disconnect legislation to help workers cope with workplace burnout.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: To help workers cope with workplace burnout, I recently asked in this House whether it was timely for us to consider a “Right to Disconnect” legislation.

sections.label: Overwork and productivity study
sections.summary: A 2014 study by Prof John Pencavel found that overworking beyond 55 hours per week causes a sharp decline in productivity per hour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to a 2014 study by Prof John Pencavel from the Stanford University, overworking beyond 55 hours per week causes a sharp decline in productivity per hour.

sections.label: Presenteeism and France legislation
sections.summary: A Global Corporate Challenge study found presenteeism reduces productivity, and France's Right to Disconnect legislation mandates employer-employee negotiation on non-emergency calls and non-critical emails outside working hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to a study by the Global Corporate Challenge, presenteeism reduces productivity and many employers have been moving away from using time spent at the office as a proxy for good performance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In France, the Right to Disconnect legislation makes it mandatory for employers and employees to negotiate on the protocol for non-emergency calls and non-critical emails outside of working hours.

sections.label: Tripartite Advisory and Right to Disconnect
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Tripartite Advisory on Mental Health will include Right to Disconnect aspects, urges MOM to conduct a yearly workplace mental health survey, and agrees with studying implementation in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: These are certainly not radical practices, but baby steps which we can easily adopt here in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: But I do agree with Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamed that we should study in greater detail how a Right to Disconnect legislation could be implemented in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: But in the meantime, I hope that the Tripartite Advisory on Mental Health – which the Senior Minister of State had assured last week would be published soon – will include aspects of the Right to Disconnect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: With clearer guidelines, our unions can start a conversation with employers on the protocol to answer non-critical work calls and emails outside of working hours, as well as the provision of appropriate help for those facing workplace burnout, while keeping their identities confidential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I also urge MOM to conduct a yearly survey on workplace mental health.

sections.label: Mandatory WSH officer
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MOM will heed repeated calls for a mandatory WSH officer at every workplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: To do so, I hope that MOM will finally heed my repeated calls for a mandatory WSH officer at every workplace.

sections.label: Micro-jobs through CDCs
sections.summary: The speaker was excited to hear Deputy Prime Minister Heng will set up an initiative to create micro-jobs in the community through CDC networks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: She is both the sole breadwinner as well as the sole care-giver in her household.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I was excited to hear from Deputy Prime Minister Heng that he will be setting up an initiative to look at creating micro-jobs in the community through the good and safe networks of our Community Development Councils or CDCs.

sections.label: Micro work protection and safety nets
sections.summary: In-community micro work may attract many women, but protection and safety nets are needed as micro-jobs move into the free market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Thus, the prospects of in-community micro work will be an attractive option for many women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, in enabling women with this option, we must be certain to be able to provide protection and safety nets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As micro-jobs pick up in popularity and leave the safe protective hands of the CDC and into the invisible hands of the free market, the House may need to consider some protective areas.

sections.label: Educating micro-jobbers and service buyers
sections.summary: As micro-jobs and non-traditional employment types come into play, micro-jobbers and their service buyers must be educated of their obligations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As micro-jobs and other non-traditional employment types come into play, we will need to educate both micro-jobbers and their service buyers of their obligations.

sections.label: Standards for micro-job payment terms
sections.summary: Without dampening the flexible nature of micro-jobs, standards are necessary for issues such as payment terms and service waivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Without dampening the spirit of the flexible nature of micro-jobs, it is necessary to look into some standards for issues such as payment terms and service waivers.

sections.label: Premium increase and MediShield Life Fund
sections.summary: An insured person paying $1,000 in annual premium will now pay $1,350, while the MediShield Life Fund has $8.3 billion in assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our population could view this act as "giving with one hand and taking with the other." Let me give you some examples that give rise to such a sentiment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: That means an insured person who used to be paying $1,000 in annual premium will now have to pay $1,350 per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While this change is under public consultation until end of October, the MediShield Life Fund already has $8.3 billion of total assets and continues to accumulate large surpluses of about $0.9 billion a year.

sections.label: ERP increase at CTE gantries
sections.summary: On 9 October, LTA announced that ERP at six gantries along the CTE would be increased from 12 October to ease peak-period congestion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, on 9 October, LTA announced that the Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) at six gantries along the CTE would be increased from 12 October to ease congestion during peak periods.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme payments to local companies
sections.summary: Of $37 billion in financial transfers, $23 billion is paid to local companies through the Jobs Support Scheme to preserve jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Of the $37 billion of financial transfers, $23 billion is paid to local companies through the Jobs Support Scheme to preserve jobs for Singaporeans and PRs.

sections.label: COVID-19 spending and financial assets
sections.summary: The $29 billion COVID-19 spending, $22 billion loan guarantees and $100 billion support measures are detailed, alongside $1.35 trillion in financial assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The $29 billion spent on fighting COVID-19 includes spending on the upgrading of testing facilities, providing new housing facilities for the foreign workers, funding projects like the $2 billion allocated to the SG Together initiative, $2 billion to the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package and $1 billion to the Jobs Growth Incentive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The $22 billion of loan guarantees are for the Government to provide guarantees of up to 90% of the loan principal for various forms of credit given by commercial banks to SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The $100 billion support measures are paid for by $18 billion of accumulated fiscal surpluses of the previous term of Government; $52 billion of drawdown from the Reserves; $8 billion of reduced current expenditure for FY2020; and $22 billion in loan capital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: According to the Deputy Prime Minister's reply to hon Member Mr Leon Perera in June this year, the $22 billion in loan capital is expected to be repaid in the future and is, hence, fiscally neutral.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In its latest Government financial statements as at end March 2020, it was reported that we own a total of $1.35 trillion in financial assets – and $1.35 trillion is $1,350 billion.

sections.label: Share of financial assets used
sections.summary: Only 1.1% of total financial assets was used to fight COVID-19 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The conclusion from all these is that we have used up only 1.1% of our total financial assets to fight COVID-19 in 2020.

sections.label: JSS jobs saved and payouts
sections.summary: The speaker declares interests in ComfortDelGro and SPWU, and states 75,000 jobs were saved by the JSS, with payouts likely exceeding $15 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Before I proceed further, Mr Speaker, Sir, I would like to declare my interest as part of the management team in ComfortDelGro and my interest as an Advisor to the Singapore Port Workers Union or SPWU.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: It is reported that 75,000 jobs were saved due to the JSS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: The total amount disbursed under JSS will likely exceed $15 billion.

sections.label: Firms declining or returning JSS
sections.summary: As at 24 September 2020, more than 700 firms declined or returned JSS payouts, after over 130 companies returned $97 million in June 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In the written reply to my Parliamentary Question last week, we understand from Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance that as at 24 September 2020, more than 700 firms have declined and/or returned JSS payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In June 2020, more than 130 companies have already returned $97 million of JSS payouts.

sections.label: Payouts denied to firms
sections.summary: 444 firms were denied payouts partially or in full, amounting to almost $10 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Of these, 444 were denied payouts either partially or in full to the tune of almost $10 million.

sections.label: CDC vouchers and COVID-19 support
sections.summary: CDC vouchers are usable only in neighbourhood shops unlike $150 vouchers for 1-room and 2-room flats, and the $100 billion support cushioned COVID-19's economic impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: CDC vouchers are unlike the $150 vouchers recently given out by the Government to families living in 1-room and 2-room flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: The latter can only be used in large supermarket chains and CDC vouchers can only be used in neighbourhood shops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: During the outbreak, the business of big supermarket chains was booming while that of neighbourhood shops was very poor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Speaker, Sir, it is clear that COVID-19 will be a part of our lives for some time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: It is thus not practical or feasible for the funding schemes that have helped Singaporeans and businesses to continue in the same form.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: But it is imperative that help still needs to be given because people and businesses are still suffering.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: The importance of the $100 billion financial support cannot be underestimated as it has helped cushion the economic impact of COVID-19 for many individuals and families.

sections.label: Key areas for Singapore economy
sections.summary: The passage lists three key areas: creating verticals eco-system under Singapore Inc., nurturing the green economy, and creating an inclusive growth workforce.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: The key areas are: one, creating key verticals eco-system under Singapore Inc.; two, nurturing the green economy; and three, creating an inclusive growth workforce On the first area, during the initial stage of COVID-19 when cases were exploding in some countries and borders begin to shut, the fault-lines in the supply chains globally were apparent.

sections.label: Fortitude test kit and resilience
sections.summary: A*Star produced the Fortitude test kit during the pandemic, showing Singapore has talent and resources to build its defence and resilience.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: During the height of the pandemic where A*Star was able to produce the Fortitude test kit and many countries were keen on having the “made in Singapore” label for items, it demonstrated that Singapore, despite being a small nation, we do have the talent pool and resources to build our line of defence and increase our resilience to the best extent possible that can weather this current health crisis and other challenges ahead.

sections.label: 30 by 30 local produce goal
sections.summary: Some areas exist today while others must be built in the future economy, with a goal of 30 by 30 local produce to supplement nutritional needs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Some exist today, but others are areas we have to begin building in our future economy.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: There is a goal of 30 by 30 local produce to supplement Singapore’s nutritional needs.

sections.label: Developing strategic industries and economies of scale
sections.summary: For strategic industries, developing existing companies to achieve economies of scale and financial strength is worthy, similar to domestic banks like DBS and OCBC.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: For such industries of strategic importance, it is worthy that we can further develop existing companies to grow to the point where substantial economies of scale can be enjoyed and thereby having the financial muscles to weather the volatile changes – similar to what has been done previously in the financial sector with our domestic banks like DBS, OCBC and their peers, and thus becoming a very key pillar in the local economy.

sections.label: Skills upgrading and low-wage workers
sections.summary: The passage asks about tracking skills upgrading statistics, notes SkillsFuture credit top-ups, and discusses barriers for low-wage and special needs groups.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Will the Government be tracking statistics of people skills upgrading in relation to job enhancement opportunities or its corresponding ability to remain in the workforce?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: The $500 to $1,000 top-up in SkillsFuture credit is useful to better enable Singaporeans to take up new courses and for them to pick up new skills.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: However, there always remains groups of individuals like the low-wage workers and special needs community who even before COVID-19, have been unable to take up courses for personal upgrades.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Their reasons for not doing so are varied, some because they have to balance multiple jobs, others care-giving duties, lack of funds or lack of suitable courses that is catered to them in language or academic qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: They are left out from being able to upgrade not due to lack of will, but more a lack of time and the need to first survive.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: For these groups, the stipend may not be adequate as the opportunity cost of forgoing a job to attend these programs are indeed high.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: With that said, I must mention that wages for the worker in some sectors at the 20th percentile in the last five years have, indeed, grown faster than the median worker as it was supported by the Progressive Wage Model or PWM.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Workfare schemes including the Special Employment Credit will also be further enhanced in January 2021 to improve their retirement adequacy through cash as well as CPF top-ups.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Further, through incorporating the skills upgrading element into justification of increasing their wages for those in the cleaning, security and landscaping industries, I think beyond this support, I look forward to the expansion of the PWM to other service sectors for more inclusion and coverage on a wider group of individuals.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Low-wage workers and even those in the special needs community struggle to find alternative jobs and may end up being displaced from the marketplace for even a longer period after the economy restarts.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: With the new and future economy, can we find avenues for more micro jobs to create for not only the seniors but also the special needs adults?

sections.label: Singapore Mental Health study findings
sections.summary: The 2016 Singapore Mental Health study found millennials aged 18 to 34 more likely to report mental health issues, with median help-seeking delays for several disorders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Singapore Mental Health study in 2016 noted that millennials between ages 18 and 34 were more likely to report experiencing a mental health issue compared to other age groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The study found that 11 years is a median time between when they first experience symptoms and when they sought help for obsessive compulsive disorder; four years for bipolar disorder and alcohol abuse; two years for generalised anxiety disorder and one year for major depressive disorder.

sections.label: National Care Hotline and taskforce
sections.summary: Singapore established a National Care Hotline in April, and PM Lee announced an inter-agency taskforce on COVID-19's psycho-social impact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Singapore saw the establishment of a National Care Hotline in April, now manned by 900 odd volunteers, which also has served over 28,000 calls by this August.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On World Mental Health Day, Prime Minister Lee has announced the establishment of an inter-agency taskforce to look at the psycho-social impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the population.

sections.label: MediSave psychiatric withdrawal limits
sections.summary: MediSave withdrawal limits are $150 per day for inpatient psychiatric treatment and $450 per day for physical treatment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For instance, MediSave withdrawal limits for inpatient psychiatric treatment is subject to a withdrawal limit of $150 per day but physical treatment is subject to the to the withdrawal limit of $450 per day.

sections.label: PSLE assessed core subjects
sections.summary: Singapore has nine core subjects, but only four are assessed in the PSLE.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, although we have nine core subjects, only four of them are assessed in the PSLE.

sections.label: Subject-based banding grouping by results
sections.summary: MOE is moving from streaming to subject-based banding, but students are still grouped by similar results in each subject.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While MOE is moving away from streaming towards subject-based banding which removes the labelling, it does not change the fact that students are still grouped based on similar results in each subject.

sections.label: PSLE age and through-train pilot
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOE to pilot through-train Primary to Secondary schools without PSLE, citing an OECD survey on fear of failure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While some feel the PSLE is necessary for Secondary school posting, there are others, like myself, who believe it is premature to assess students at the age of 12 to determine their educational paths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I therefore urge MOE to consider a pilot project of through-train schools from Primary to Secondary levels without going through the PSLE, to give parents the option to choose an education path that may be better suited for their children's future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In an OECD survey, it was found that three in four Singapore students fear failure as compared to a global average of 55%.

sections.label: Assessments and learning value of failing
sections.summary: Assessments should account for the learning value of failing by giving students multiple opportunities to try again.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Assessments should take into account the learning value of failing by giving them multiple opportunities to try again.

sections.label: Education officers and NIE intake
sections.summary: Education officers fell from 36,400 in 2016 to 33,700 in 2018, and NIE intake fell from 1,256 to 556.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The number of education officers dropped from 36,400 in 2016 to 33,700 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The NIE intake dropped from 1,256 in 2016 to 556 in 2018.

sections.label: Foreign students and university revenues
sections.summary: Foreign students contributed 11.9 billion pounds in the UK in 2016 and $37.6 billion in Australia in 2019, and Singapore could adopt a similar model.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In UK, these students contributed 11.9 billion pounds to the UK economy in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In Australia, they contributed $37.6 billion to the Australian economy in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: With good global rankings, our Universities should similarly be able to attract full fee-paying foreign students.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We can adopt a similar model, develop this industry and use the revenues to further subsidise the education of local students.

sections.label: Q4 2020 tariff fuel cost increase
sections.summary: The increase in Q4 2020 tariffs is primarily due to fuel cost increases, with Brent crude oil price rising 47% between July and September.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The increase in Q4 2020 tariffs are primarily due to fuel cost increases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Perhaps to share a little bit more, between July and September, in this same quarter, the crude oil price, Brent crude oil price, went up by a whooping 47%.

sections.label: GST Voucher U-Save doubled
sections.summary: The GST Voucher U-Save was doubled this year through a one-off special payment, and eligible HDB households with five or more members received further rebates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: On top of that, the GST Voucher - U-Save has also been doubled this year through a one-off a one-off GST Voucher - U-Save special payment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Eligible HDB households with five or more members also received a first tranche of further GST Voucher - U-Save rebates of between $60 and $100 per household in October.

sections.label: Households switching to Open Electricity Market
sections.summary: About 48% of all households have already switched over to the Open Electricity Market retailer.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: On top of that, in my reply to the question that hon Member Liang Eng Hwa had asked, I have also said that close to 50% – about 48%, to be exact – of all of our households have already switched over to the Open Electricity market retailer.

sections.label: SP Group returns and grid infrastructure
sections.summary: EMA calculates a fair rate of return for SP Group's assets, separate from wholesale electricity prices, for the grid infrastructure it has put in place.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: SP Group's returns, how that is determined – the Energy Market Authority or EMA, as the regulator, will then look at the assets that the SP Group has put in place and calculate what is the fair rate of return for those assets.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: It is actually separate from the price of electricity in the wholesale market.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: That is not what the SP Group earns.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: SP Group is the entity that transmits the electrons.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: They earn a return for the infrastructure that they have put in place, the grid infrastructure that they have put in place.

sections.label: Singapore as global-Asia tech node
sections.summary: Singapore is to be remade as a global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise, with digital as a game-changer and a domestic eco-system as home base.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: First, re-making Singapore as a global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise with digital as a game-changer, while building up our domestic eco-system as a home base for innovation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Second, preparing Singaporeans for the digital world and doing this at scale.

sections.label: Industry transformation maps progress
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Heng spoke on progress implementing industry transformation maps to restructure the economy sector by sector, firm by firm, affecting 23 sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng, in his speech, spoke about the progress made with the implementation of our industry transformation maps (ITMs) to restructure our economy, sector by sector, firm by firm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: This transformation is important as it affects 23 sectors and our businesses within these sectors.

sections.label: Global tech giants in Singapore
sections.summary: Global technology giants making Singapore their Asian headquarters, with Singapore as a regional hub for technology and start-ups, creates quality jobs, talent and know-how.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Having global technology giants, like Google, Microsoft, Amazon, LinkedIn, Facebook and, more recently, the best Chinese tech companies, Alibaba, BtyeDance and Tencent, making Singapore their Asian headquarters and base for their operations in the region, coupled with Singapore becoming a regional and global hub for technology and start-ups not only creates quality jobs – and this is very important because we need quality jobs for Singaporeans – but it brings with it talent and, more importantly, know-how that creates a vibrancy and a buzz to drive innovations and investments.

sections.label: COVID-19 and digital skills training
sections.summary: COVID-19 accelerated this, so platforms are needed to train large groups of experienced workers in new skills, especially digital, iteratively as technology and workforce keep moving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: And COVID-19 has just accelerated this even more.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: So, what we need to do is to have platforms for training large groups of experienced people in the workforce to build new skills, especially digital skills, and this process needs to be iterative because technology and changes in the workforce will continue to keep moving and it is not static.

sections.label: Educational institutions mutual recognition
sections.summary: Development programmes are in silos, so educational institutions must come together for training programmes and endorsements supporting mutual recognition of prior learning to accelerate quality learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Many different institutions provide development programmes but they are in silos.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: We must get educational institutions to come together for training programmes and endorsements of each other's training programmes to support a mutual recognition of prior learning so that we can accelerate the learning because what we need is speed but not speed in just getting it done, but quality.

sections.label: Policy framework for continuous learning
sections.summary: Making this happen at scale requires a policy framework bringing companies, training institutions and the workforce together to address demand, accelerate training and encourage continuous learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: To make this happen at scale will require the policy framework – most importantly to bring stakeholders together, meaning companies, training institutions and people in the workforce to address demand, accelerate training and encourage experienced people to want to learn – what I call a culture of continuous curiousity in learning.

sections.label: Government Smart Nation investment
sections.summary: The Government should keep driving Smart Nation efforts by investing in open infrastructure, business-friendly policies, and data and cybersecurity laws.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In today's context where digital is critical for resilience and agility, it is even more important that the Government continues to drive and strengthen Singapore's Smart Nation efforts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Investing in state-of-the-art open and connected infrastructure, business friendly environment, policies, intellectual property, data and cybersecurity laws will provide the eco-system for people and businesses to thencome together to create value.

sections.label: Digital capability of workforce
sections.summary: Singapore must keep investing in the eco-system to develop its workforce's digital capability for post-COVID-19 opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: To do so, Singapore must continue to invest in the eco-system to develop the digital capability of our workforce to be ready for the opportunities that do exist in the post-COVID-19 world.

sections.label: Draws on past reserves
sections.summary: The $52 billion draw was the largest ever, 13 times the 2009 draw, with no legal obligation to restore it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At $52 billion, these were the largest ever draws on past reserves – 13 times what was drawn in 2009 during the Global Financial Crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: During the debate on his Ministerial Statement in June, the Deputy Prime Minister clarified that there is no legal or constitutional obligation for the Government to restore the draw from past reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, he said that the Government is committed to rebuilding the reserves, although he said that the Government cannot be definitive about how long that would take.

sections.label: Reserves restoration timeline costs
sections.summary: Restoring reserves over two years would need $26 billion yearly, impossible given the highest surplus was $10.9 billion in FY2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, a restoration timeline of two years will require the provision of $26 billion a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is clearly impossible even in the best of times, as the Government's highest ever Budget surplus was $10.9 billion in FY2017, which was an exceptional year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Even a timeline of 30 years will still require a provision of $1.7 billion a year on average.

sections.label: Fall in passenger traffic
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Heng said passenger traffic fell by more than 98% in August compared with last year, affecting many Singaporeans' livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As Deputy Prime Minister Heng has shared in his Ministerial Statement, compared with last year, passenger traffic has fallen by more than 98% in August.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This has had a huge impact on the livelihoods of many Singaporeans.

sections.label: Tan family income drop
sections.summary: Mr Tan drives a taxi and Mrs Tan is a tour agent, and their family faces more than a 50% drop in income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Tan family – Mr Tan drives a taxi and Mrs Tan is a tour agent whose family has to deal with more than 50% drop in their income.

sections.label: PMETs and job redesign
sections.summary: Six of 10 Singaporeans work as PMETs, and the past six months were the biggest exercise in redesigning jobs and reassessing how work is defined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With six of 10 of us Singaporeans working as PMETs, the past six months have been the biggest exercise in redesigning jobs and reassessing the way we define work.

sections.label: Tripartite group and Progressive Wage Model
sections.summary: COVID-19, new technology and digitalisation will cause structural changes, unemployment and pressure on lower wage workers, so the Tripartite Working Group should expedite the Progressive Wage Model across other sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: COVID-19, new technology and digitalisation will also bring about structural changes that will give rise to unemployment and place greater pressure on the vulnerable lower wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, it is important that the Tripartite Working Group, comprising of MOM, NTUC and SNEF, work together to expedite the implementation of the Progressive Wage Model across other sectors.

sections.label: Electric cars and lower wage workers
sections.summary: As Singapore moves to electric cars and phases out internal combustion engines, the Progressive Wage Model with Workfare Skills Support, ComCare and KiFAS can help affected lower wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As we move from hybrid to electric cars with our goal of phasing out vehicles with internal combustion engines, what will happen to these pump attendants, petrol station clerks and similar lower wage workers in industries that are undergoing transformation even as I speak?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This is where the Progressive Wage Model complemented by the Workfare Skills Support Scheme and other needs-based social safety nets such as ComCare and KiFAS will be able to help lower wage workers with needs-based support.

sections.label: Employees wanting remote working
sections.summary: An EngageRocket study with Singapore Human Resource Institute and Human Resource Professionals showed nine of 10 employees want to continue some form of remote working.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: A study by EngageRocket, in partnership with Singapore Human Resource Institute and Human Resource Professionals showed that nine of 10 employees shared that they would like to continue with some form of remote working as a new way of working.

sections.label: Decks Pte Ltd e-commerce sales
sections.summary: Decks Pte Ltd, cited by Deputy Prime Minister Heng, increased its sales tenfold after it revamped its e-commerce platform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Take for example, the company cited by Deputy Prime Minister Heng, Decks Pte Ltd which increased its sales tenfold after it revamped its e-commerce platform.

sections.label: Lean Six Sigma Blackbelt course subsidy
sections.summary: A Lean Six Sigma Blackbelt course requires attendees to prove improvements driving a $1 million cost saving to receive the course subsidy and certification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: One example is a course I attended on Lean Six Sigma Blackbelt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is an operational excellence course and in order to receive the course subsidy and certification, the attendee will have to prove that he has brought improvements to drive a $1 million cost saving for the organisation.

sections.label: Redesigning jobs for inclusive growth
sections.summary: Working from home has changed the employment structure, so jobs should be re-designed to give inclusive growth opportunities to older and less able workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For example, working from home has changed the employment structure We have to learn from this experience and re-design jobs to provide inclusive growth opportunities for older and less able workers.

sections.label: Supporting vulnerable workers and competitiveness
sections.summary: Structural changes will cause job losses and pressure on vulnerable workers, so the Tripartite Working Group should be supported and the Progressive Wage Model accelerated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Structural changes will cause workers to lose their jobs and exert greater pressure on workers who are more vulnerable to these changes We should support the Tripartite Working Group.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We need to accelerate the implementation of the Progressive Wage Model for certain industries and provide opportunities for more vulnerable groups of workers to upgrade their skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Competition for PMET jobs is no longer limited to Singapore alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This means that the question of foreign worker quotas becomes less relevant when compared to the need to ensure that Singaporeans remain competitive in the global job market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: To ensure that we remain competitive in the global market, we need to have the right skills, the right way of thinking and the ability to seize the opportunities available We need to equip our workforce with soft skills, such as change management, to implement changes at work.

sections.label: Climate pledge amid COVID crisis
sections.summary: Besides Paris Agreement timelines and obligations, Singapore must keep addressing the climate emergency and cannot let COVID delay its pledge of a 36% emissions intensity cut by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This is not merely because we have timelines and obligations under the Paris Agreement, we also have to keep playing our part to address the climate emergency in the meantime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We cannot afford to let COVID crisis distract, delay or derail us from our pledge to the 36% cut on emissions intensity by 2030.

sections.label: Support for vulnerable self-employed workers
sections.summary: DPM Heng Swee Keat said the Government is studying support for the most vulnerable self-employed workers and will update before year end.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Last Monday Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat said in his Ministerial Statement that the Government is studying the support for the self-employed workers who are most vulnerable and will provide an update before the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In some of the SIRS cases I did for my residents, I noticed that cases have, for example, been rejected if in the previous year the applicants have been earning salary of more than $2,300 dollars a month or who have not been earning trade income.

sections.label: Reasons self-employed support rejected
sections.summary: Others were turned away because their spouse's income exceeded $70,000 last year or their condo's annual value exceeded the limit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Others were turned away because their spouse recorded income of more than $70,000 last year or the annual value of their condo has exceeded the annual value limit.

sections.label: Baby grant start date concerns
sections.summary: Parents with Singaporean children born 1 October 2021 to 30 September 2022 can get a one-off $3,000 grant, but a resident whose baby was born in August is baffled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Next, the Government has announced last week that parents with Singaporean children born from 1 October this year to 30 September 2022 can get a one-off $3,000 grant to help them defray the costs of raising a child amid the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: He and his wife just had their first baby in August this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: They are baffled that the grant will only apply to parents with children born from 1 October.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: My resident told me that if the purpose of this grant is to encourage new births amidst the crisis, then the grants should apply to births in nine or 10 months from this month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: He emphasised by that having the start date from 1 October, it has "selectively ignored parents who were impacted the most as we do face the same problems or even more than those parents who have their babies from 1 October".

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: He asked, "why were they included for the support and us, who had our babies months earlier, were neglected?" He felt disheartened that "the Government has chosen to ignore us who are directly impacted by the pandemic." I hope that the Government will extend the grant to all children born from the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, for example, from February 2020 onwards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Parents who gave birth to children in this period had to bare the brunt of the difficult challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: Retrenched worker at Meet-the-People Session
sections.summary: A retrenched sales worker now drives for Grab and does not qualify for the SIRS scheme because of his housing type.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: He came to see me at the Meet-the-People Session.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: He was recently retrenched from his five-figure monthly salary sales job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: He was hoping to find one with a salary of a few thousand dollars for his family to survive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: He is now a Grab driver and he does not qualify for the SIRS scheme because of his housing type.

sections.label: Government resources for job redesign
sections.summary: One way is for the Government to dedicate more resources to job redesign initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One way is for the Government to dedicate more resources to the job redesign initiatives.

sections.label: Tripartite work group on low-income workers
sections.summary: A new tripartite work group is being formed to improve salaries and well-being of low-income workers without risking job losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the same vein of using a targeted approach, it is heartening to learn that a new tripartite work group is being formed to look into improving the salaries and well-being of low-income workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this way, we work towards increasing their wages and accessibility to training opportunities without risking the loss of jobs.

sections.label: Extension and tapering of JSS
sections.summary: The JSS extension to March 2021 is supported with tapering, and next payouts are in October 2020 and March 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The extension of the JSS to March 2021 is a strategic necessity and I support the tapering of the JSS to ensure fiscal prudence as we look towards the long-term growth of the Singapore economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The next JSS payouts will be made in October 2020 and March 2021, with a six-month gap in between.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Maps review
sections.summary: The ITMs, launched in Budget 2016 as industry-specific roadmaps, are being reviewed for relevance and effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Industry Transformation Maps or ITMs were first launched as part of a $4.5 billion industry transformation package in Budget 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: They were industry-specific roadmaps which aimed to take an integrated approach where trade associations and chambers, companies and the Government worked together to help each sector prepare for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These ITMs are currently being reviewed to ensure relevance and effectiveness.

sections.label: Taskforce on low-wage worker wages
sections.summary: Minister Josephine Teo mentioned a new taskforce that will explore ways to raise wages of low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Minister Josephine Teo mentioned about the formation of a new taskforce that will explore ways to raise the wages of our low-wage workers.

sections.label: NUS science and arts integration
sections.summary: The proposed integration of NUS's Faculty of Science with the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences will include design as a compulsory core module.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Even the recently announced proposed integration of the Faculty of Science with the Faculty of the Arts and Social Sciences at NUS will see design as one of the compulsory core modules.

sections.label: DBS passbook ATMs for seniors
sections.summary: DBS created BTMs so seniors can scan passbooks to withdraw cash and update passbooks without waiting for a counter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: DBS discovered that many senior residents were still queuing in their branches to withdraw cash because they value the traditional passbook over card-based ATMs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, DBS created the BTMs where seniors can simply scan their passbooks to withdraw cash and still have their passbooks updated without having to wait for a physical counter to be available.

sections.label: Design Singapore Masterplan strategic update
sections.summary: The passage suggests the Design Singapore Council could strategically update the 2016 Singapore Design Masterplan given changes in two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Our public service needs to embrace design in significant ways, too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This could also be the right time for Design Singapore Council to undertake a strategic update of the Singapore Design Masterplan that was launched in 2016, considering how much has changed in just the last two years.

sections.label: Workfare payouts and ITMs
sections.summary: An interim JSS payout in December will aid this, ITMs should ensure upskilling and job re-design, and WSP of $3,000 is being paid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Enhancing the next phase of JSS with an interim payout in December will aid in this endeavour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In addition, the new ITMs should also ensure the upskilling and job re-design of our low-wage workers while ensuring business sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: During Budget 2020, it was announced that Singaporeans who had been receiving the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) payments for work done in 2019 will receive a Workfare Special Payment (WSP) of $3,000 in 2020, with the second tranche being paid out this month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Since the implementation of WIS in 2007, Singaporeans aged 35 and above in the bottom 20th-30th percentile of the workforce has received over $5.5 billion in support.

sections.label: Lowering WIS age eligibility
sections.summary: The Government must study if this assumption still holds and consider lowering the age eligibility to 30 for WIS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Government must study if this assumption still holds and consider lowering the age eligibility to 30 years old for workers to qualify for WIS.

sections.label: Same WIS payout across age groups
sections.summary: The Government should consider making WIS payouts the same across age groups based on income, so equal salaries get equal payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Another improvement to WIS is for the Government to consider having the payout to be the same across different age groups, based on the worker’s income, meaning that a 35- or 65-year-old worker earning the same salary, will receive the same payout quantum.

sections.label: Extending Jobs Support Scheme
sections.summary: The Government should consider extending the JSS beyond March 2021, especially in industries more keenly feeling COVID-19's impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: While this should be commended, the Government should consider extending the JSS beyond March 2021 especially in industries where the impact of COVID-19 is more keenly felt.

sections.label: Singapore economy third quarter contraction
sections.summary: MTI advance estimates show the Singapore economy contracted 7% year-on-year in Q3 2020, improving from the 13.3% contraction in Q2.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Based on MTI’s advance estimates released today, the Singapore economy contracted by 7% on a year-on-year basis in the third quarter of 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This was an improvement from the 13.3% contraction in the second quarter and came on the back of the phased re-opening of our economy following the circuit breaker.

sections.label: Businesses resuming operations
sections.summary: About 95% of businesses are now allowed to resume operations and more people are returning to office.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: About 95% of businesses are now allowed to resume operations and more people are returning to office.

sections.label: ESG loan scheme take-up
sections.summary: As of September 2020, more than 18,000 enterprises have taken up loans under ESG's loan scheme, such as the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: For instance, our loan schemes have helped firms to address immediate cash flow issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: I want to update the House that as of September 2020, more than 18,000 enterprises have taken up loans under the ESG’s loan scheme, such as the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme.

sections.label: ESG supported projects
sections.summary: Since the start of this year, ESG has supported over 28,000 projects under these schemes to help companies increase productivity, build capabilities and expand overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Since the start of this year, ESG has supported over 28,000 projects under these schemes to help our companies increase productivity, build new capabilities and expand overseas.

sections.label: Support for firms by sector
sections.summary: Firms are grouped into three buckets: good growth prospects, temporary demand drop, and permanently changed sectors, each receiving different support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: First, for the firms in sectors with good growth prospects, such as biomedical manufacturing, we will help them scale faster and create more jobs for our workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: For firms the second bucket where they are in sectors that are facing a temporary drop in demand due to COVID-19 but will eventually recover, such as F&B and aerospace manufacturing, we will help them to preserve capabilities, consolidate capacity and tide them through this period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Third, for firms in sectors which have changed permanently, such as social entertainment, we will help them to pivot into new markets and businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: I just wanted to say that since March 2020, pubs, bars, nightclubs, discotheques and karaoke lounges have not been allowed to operate as their operations pose higher risks of transmission arising from prolonged contact over a period of time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: But I wanted to assure the House that the Government has been in consultation with the night life industry and we are finalising the support measures to assist them with the affected firms and employees and we will announce more details shortly.

sections.label: Digital Economy Agreements signed
sections.summary: Singapore signed its first two Digital Economy Agreements this year with Chile, New Zealand and Australia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Singapore signed its first two Digital Economy Agreements this year with Chile, New Zealand and also with Australia.

sections.label: Government support for worker skills
sections.summary: The Government will support workers picking up new skills through SkillsFuture Credit programmes, SGUnited Jobs and Skills package and WSG's Professional Conversion Programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: And as a Government, we will support our workers as they pick up new skills and prepare for new opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We have been doing so through the SkillsFuture Credit programmes under SGUnited Jobs and Skills package and WSG's Professional Conversion Programmes or PCPs.

sections.label: Business credits and hiring incentives
sections.summary: Businesses can use SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit for workforce transformation, and the Jobs Growth Incentive provides salary support to encourage hiring of local employees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: For instance, businesses can use the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit to cover their expenses on workforce transformation initiatives, including job redesigning and training for workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: The Jobs Growth Incentive also provides salary support to encourage businesses especially those which are expanding, to hire more local employees, which the Minister for Manpower had mentioned earlier.

sections.label: SSIA worker placements in electronics
sections.summary: Since 2016, SSIA has facilitated placement of over 1,200 workers into the electronics industry through the programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Since 2016, SSIA has facilitated the placement of over 1,200 workers into the electronics industry through the programme.

sections.label: BH Global fever screening equipment
sections.summary: Local SME BH Global produces mass fever screening equipment used at Changi Airport, now deployed in major airports worldwide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: One of these local SME is BH Global.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: The mass fever screening equipment that you see at Changi Airport is locally produced by them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, it is being deployed worldwide in major airports in Europe, US, UK, India, Kuwait and many more.

sections.label: Sports Singapore and Dow shoe upcycling
sections.summary: Sports Singapore and Dow collaborate to upcycle 300,000 pairs of used shoes into sports infrastructure, as building and construction account for 39% of global carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: One such example is the collaboration between Sports Singapore and Dow to upcycle 300,000 pairs of used shoes into sports infrastructure, such as jogging tracks, fitness areas and playgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: According to the World Green Building Council, building and construction account for 39% of all carbon emissions in the world and with buildings' operational emission accounting for 28%.

sections.label: Global infection and death totals
sections.summary: Globally, 38 million people are infected and 1.09 million people have died.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Globally, the number stands at 38 million infected people and 1.09 million people have died.

sections.label: Singapore COVID-19 efforts and support
sections.summary: Efforts kept fatality rates low, testing high, medical capacity expanded, and support measures helped businesses and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As a result of all these efforts, although we had a spike in cases, largely from a combination of Singaporeans returning from abroad as well as a spread in the dormitories, fatality rates were kept low and are amongst the lowest in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our testing rates are now amongst the highest as a percentage of the population and we had expanded our medical capacity so that everyone who needed medical attention would be able to get it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The wide range of measures provided – from jobs support packages for employers, rental reliefs for businesses and supplementary income for both employees and the self-employed – has provided many Singaporean businesses the ability to stay afloat and provided many Singaporeans with money to spend even if their income has dropped.

sections.label: Low interest rates and jobs
sections.summary: Low interest rates keep borrowing costs lower for businesses, and the National Jobs Council curated 117,500 opportunities as at end of August.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The low interest rate environment is also helpful as this keeps the cost of borrowing lower for businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I would also like to congratulate the National Jobs Council for curating 117,500 opportunities as at end of August.

sections.label: Global-Asia node of technology
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister's statement emphasised developing Singapore into a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise supported by an inclusive workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister's statement emphasised developing Singapore into a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise which will be supported by a strong, skilled and yet inclusive workforce.

sections.label: Support for disadvantaged and underprivileged
sections.summary: SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centres, the COVID-19 Support Grant, household support schemes are helpful, but more should be done for underprivileged children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, I appreciate that SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centres in the HDB estates will reach out to the disadvantaged ones to help with job matching.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The extension of the COVID-19 Support Grant and the continued support for households, such as the GST Voucher, Grocery Vouchers, Service and Conservancy Charges or S&CC rebates, and Workfare Special Payment, are also helpful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, there is room for us to do more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I appeal to the Government and its agencies to make an additional effort to provide a better living and learning environment for the underprivileged children.

sections.label: Lost Einsteins and innovation
sections.summary: An analysis of patents by 1.2 million Americans found children of the top 1% are 10 times more likely to be inventors, and lost Einsteins could quadruple US innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: An analysis of the patents filed by 1.2 million Americans found that children of the top 1% are 10 times more likely to be inventors than equally smart kids from other backgrounds...if...children from low-income families could invent at the same rate... these 'lost Einsteins' could quadruple innovation in the US.” I would venture that we can expect a similar situation in Singapore with regard to our future in innovation.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model expansion
sections.summary: The Government will expand the Progressive Wage Model to more sectors to help lower-income workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For workers in the lower income brackets, Government will help them by expanding the implementation of the Progressive Wage Model or PWM to more sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The cleaning, landscaping and security sectors have already seen the fulfilment of the four objectives of PWM, namely, career progression, skills upgrading, higher productivity and wage increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hopefully, more sectors will follow, such as for the waste management, construction, retail, food and beverage, accommodation and hospitality sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With the PWM, we can look forward to attracting more Singaporeans to work in these essential jobs and becoming less dependent on foreigners.

sections.label: Higher wages and respect
sections.summary: Workers will be paid higher wages and respected as professionals in their own right.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Workers will be paid higher wages and be respected as professionals in their own right.

sections.label: Baby Support Grant newborns
