sections.summary: A one-off $3,000 Baby Support Grant helps parents of Singaporean children born between 1 October 2020 and 30 September 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Next, I welcome the one-off $3,000 Baby Support Grant or BSG, for newborns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The BSG is intended to help parents of Singaporean children born between 1 October 2020 and 30 September 2022 to defray the cost of raising a child amid the pandemic, and hopefully, to also encourage couples not to delay parenthood.

sections.label: Extending Baby Support Grant
sections.summary: The speaker appeals to extend the $3,000 Baby Support Grant to all Singaporean babies born in 2020, including those of single mothers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Many couples also could not have their parents visit and help out due to safety measures during the circuit breaker period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I appeal to the Government to consider extending the $3,000 Baby Support Grant to all Singaporean babies born in 2020 so that we can better support our young families in these very trying times.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope babies born to single mothers can also be included to help reduce stress for the mother in an already very challenging situation.

sections.label: Selective foreigner entry call
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to bring in only foreigners with specialised skills less commonly found in the local workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: If we were to keep our goal of being an open, global and regional hub, we need to accept the presence of international firms and foreigners living and working with us in our society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: But I wish to call upon the Government to be more selective and ensure that only foreigners with specialised skills or experience that are less commonly found in our local workforce are brought into Singapore so that our citizens will feel more secure and can be convinced that the foreigners are here to add value and not compete for their jobs and other resources.

sections.label: Automation and job displacement
sections.summary: Reports project job displacement and automation growth in Singapore, with wholesale, retail, manufacturing and transport most affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A Cisco Oxford Economic Study in 2018 projected the following: 85,000 existing roles will disappear from the labour market, pushing workers into other industries and occupations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore is said, according to this report, to confront a gap in average skill levels of 14.3 on a scale of 0 to 100 – higher than Vietnam at 13.4, Malaysia at 12.7 and Thailand at 8.5.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to this report, the three sectors in line for most displacement in Singapore are: firstly, wholesale and retail with 80,000 jobs displaced; secondly, manufacturing with 55,000 jobs displaced; and thirdly, transport with 50,000 jobs displaced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Also, the 2017 Global Future of Works Survey by Willis Towers Watson found that companies in Singapore expect automation will account for an average of 29% of all work done the next three years, a big increase in 14% of work being done using automation in 2018 and just 7% in 2015.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow job placements
sections.summary: Under Adapt and Grow, including PCP and CSP, over 31,000 local jobseekers were placed in jobs in 2019, similar to 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the Adapt and Grow initiative, including PCP and CSP, more than 31,000 local jobseekers were placed in jobs in 2019, similar to the 2018 number.

sections.label: Fixed term foreign work passes
sections.summary: Economic agencies could offer limited term foreign work passes for specialised skills, with employers expected to hire a Singaporean when the term ends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In order to attract and support such investment projects that create jobs, either from foreign investors or from domestic investors and entrepreneurs, can our economic agencies offer limited term foreign work passes for individuals with such specialised skills?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To attract big investment projects in a competitive investment climate, a mix of fixed term and non-fixed term Employment Passes could be offered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For the fixed term passes, the idea would be that the employer would be expected to hire a Singaporean to fill that position when the term of the pass ends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: That fixed term, say, five years could then be used to set up training for Singaporeans to acquire those skills.

sections.label: Scandinavian workforce shift
sections.summary: Some economists argue Scandinavian economies shifted large workforce sections, such as Sweden's obsolete shipyards, to more productive skilled occupations, speeding economic upgrading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some economists have argued that the Scandinavian economies succeeded in shifting big sections of their workforce – for example, in Sweden's obsolete shipyards – to more productive skilled occupations, thereby facilitating the upgrading of the Swedish economy at a much faster and more durable pace.

sections.label: Skills upgrading and income support
sections.summary: Workers learning new skills are buoyed by a safety net with generous jobless benefits, and Singapore will need to up its game in skills upgrading and interim structural income support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Moreover, while unemployed and learning new skills, workers are buoyed by a safety net that includes generous jobless benefits." Sir, going forward, Singapore will need to seriously up its game in both skills upgrading and interim structural income support with the latter tied to the former.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Denmark's national skills anticipation system, for example, seeks to compile accessible and detailed information on labour market trends and skills demand for 850 occupations in order to: firstly, support the work of job centres in helping individuals find better job opportunities; and secondly, to informed education, employment and skills policies.

sections.label: UK work coaches
sections.summary: In the UK, around 13,500 work coaches and job centres aim to move jobseekers on benefits or income support into employment, with one coach following each claimant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the UK, for example, around 13,500 work coaches and job centres hired by the department for work and pensions aim to move jobseekers on benefits or income support into employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A single work coach will follow a claimant throughout their time on benefit, helping to match claimants to jobs that suit their skills and help to fill skill gaps by offering training to claimants who require it.

sections.label: Preparing for coming wave
sections.summary: The speaker says it behoves us to prepare for the coming wave by considering fixed term foreign work passes, jobs anticipation programmes and end-to-end KPI-driven jobs coaching.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And thus has it always been when cars replaced horses, when electric power replaced gas lighting and so on and so forth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It behoves us to prepare for that coming wave by considering ideas, like fixed term foreign work passes, jobs anticipation programmes and end-to-end KPI-driven jobs coaching.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is also good to hear the Government reiterate its commitment towards supporting Singaporeans who aspire to get married and have children.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, the policy start date of 1 October this year has meant that parents with newborns today do not benefit from the grant.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Can we consider extending this grant to parents with children born since the onset of the pandemic?

sections.label: Marriage and Parenthood Package cost
sections.summary: The Marriage and Parenthood Package costs about $4 billion a year, yet the 2019 Total Fertility Rate was 1.19, far below the replacement rate of 2.1.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Marriage and Parenthood Package is also stated to cost the Government approximately $4 billion a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, in 2019, our Total Fertility Rate was 1.19, and appears to be on course to stubbornly remain far below the replacement rate of 2.1 and still ranks amongst the lowest in the world.

sections.label: Workers' Party shared parental leave
sections.summary: The Workers' Party called for enhanced shared parental leave of 24 weeks, with a minimum of 12 weeks for the mother.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As a first step, the Workers' Party has called for enhanced shared parental leave of a total of 24 weeks that would allow couples to decide how best to split the care of their newborn child, with a minimum of 12 weeks to be given to the mother.

sections.label: Scant parental burnout research
sections.summary: There have been scant studies and time-use surveys on parents in Singapore and little research on parental burnout.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But anyone who has had to spend any amount of time being responsible for a young child would quickly debunk these ideas.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, there have been scant studies and time-use surveys done on parents in Singapore and there is also little research on parental burnout.

sections.label: Education system and childbearing anxiety
sections.summary: The high stakes education system has created anxiety around raising children and is cited as a reason families have fewer kids.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To add to the mix, our unforgiving and high stakes education system has created significant anxiety around raising children and is cited as a reason why families hold off on having kids or have fewer kids.

sections.label: Single parents and Newborn Support Grant
sections.summary: The speaker asks if single parents will be eligible for the Newborn Support Grant and whether they can be included.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Regardless of whether we believe such family structures should be encouraged, their children are innocent and better support for their parents only benefit these children.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to ask for a clarification from the Minister if single parents too will be eligible for the Newborn Support Grant, and if not, whether they can be included.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To close, the $3,000 of additional payment for families is a welcome.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, the effectiveness of this policy is limited by the extent to which the Government is willing to lean in to encourage and foster greater gender equity in the home and drive more flexibility in the workplace.

sections.label: Deputy Prime Minister on jobs and skills
sections.summary: A critical message in the Deputy Prime Minister's speech focused on jobs and building human capital by prioritising skills.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: One critical message in Deputy Prime Minister’s speech was a strong focus on jobs and in building our human capital through prioritising skills.

sections.label: SGUnited Traineeships and apprenticeships
sections.summary: The speaker cites SGUnited Traineeships and SGUnited Jobs and Skills as examples linking skilling to industry needs and requests more apprenticeship programmes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The SGUnited Traineeships programme and SGUnited Jobs and Skills package are good examples of the close relationship between in skilling our workforce to meet the actual needs of the industry.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: A number of my students are in this programme and so far, their experience has been very positive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This gives me confidence to request further that we create more apprenticeship programmes so that this notion of work and relevance becomes a mainstay in our overall education to employment pathway.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This can be in the form self-development, to break the monotony of work, or a form of further upskilling to increase their value in the profession.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We could, for instance, mandate a protected time of half a day during the work week so that our workers can take on courses and enhance their skill sets.

sections.label: Digital access and literacy
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government ensures all Singaporeans, including the elderly and children, have access to devices and are digitally literate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It has allowed many of us to work, study and remain connected.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But in that aspect, I hope that the Government pull all stops to ensure that all Singaporeans, including the elderly and our children, have access to devices and are digitally literate.

sections.label: Subject-based banding and PSLE
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes subject-based banding but says PSLE remains the elephant in the room and asks what the alternative is.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Coming from the Normal stream, I am heartened that our education system has shifted to the subject-based banding, concurrently slaying one sacred cow.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: However, the elephant in the room remains, and that is your PSLE.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: If we do do away with PSLE, what is the alternative?

sections.label: Shift to PE, Arts, Music
sections.summary: The speaker, a PE teacher, welcomes the shift of focus to PE, the Arts and Music and says COVID-19 exposed teachers' strengths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Being a physical education or PE teacher myself, I am heartened to see the shift of focus from the more academic subjects to PE, to the Arts and even Music.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I am confident that having laid such solid foundations in our education system, it has prepared us sufficiently for the future.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This COVID-19 situation has exposed the strengths of our teachers.

sections.label: Cross-border capital decline
sections.summary: The McKinsey Global Institute observed cross-border capital fell from 12% of global output to a little more than 7%, and global banks divested at least $2 trillion in assets.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Several years ago, the McKinsey Global Institute observed that cross-border capital fell from 12% of global output for the decade until 2010 to a little more than 7% since then.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Global banks, especially those in advanced economies, have divested at least $2 trillion in assets.

sections.label: Fraying global trading regime
sections.summary: The passage states international trade collapsed, global merchandise exchange fell to about 44% of global GDP, and Singapore's goods trade share fell over 40%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The aftermath saw a massive collapse in international trade and despite fitful starts and stops, global merchandise exchange has pulled back from peaks of more than half of global GDP to about 44% last year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The global trading regime is fraying with the World Trade Organization operating a dysfunctional dispute resolution system and repeated violations of open trading principles by major economic powers, most notably in the Sino-American trade war of 2018 and 2019.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our trade in goods as a share of income, fell by more than 40% over the past decade and these trends are hardly positive, with the growth of non-oil exports dipping into negative territory through most of 2019, way before the pandemic visited our shores.

sections.label: Startup SG Founder and tool kits
sections.summary: Programmes like Startup SG Founder, Enterprise Leadership for Transformation and business tool kits can be more proactive in identifying and approaching qualifying individuals and firms, especially in lagging industries.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Programmes of this nature such as Startup SG Founder, Enterprise Leadership for Transformation and various business tool kits can be made more proactive in identifying and approaching qualifying individuals and firms, especially in industries that have lagged in terms of adoption.

sections.label: Trainee expansion and placement rate
sections.summary: The passage asks how much is being expanded per trainee and what the placement rate is for programme graduates.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: How much are we expanding per a trainee, and what is the placement rate for programme graduates?

sections.label: iTalent and iSkills participation rate
sections.summary: iTalent and iSkills are one way forward, but participation involving a few dozen firms remains a drop in the ocean.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our iTalent and iSkills programmes are one such way forward, but the current participation rate, involving a few dozen firms, remain a drop in the ocean.

sections.label: Fintech reporting and Lucky Plaza policy
sections.summary: Finance start-ups face reporting requirements comparable to establishing comments and find regulator standards impossibly stringent, while a Lucky Plaza hawker said an odd-or-even IC number policy decimated foot traffic.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For example, finance start-ups often find themselves held to reporting requirements comparable to those of establishing comments, while there have been occasional initiatives toward easing pilot regulatory sandboxes as well as easier ACRA reporting requirements during COVID-19, executives from a number of fintech start-ups I have spoken to, reveal that they still find these standards that regulators hold them to, impossibly stringent.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One owner of a hawker stall in Lucky Plaza, for example, shared with me about how recent policy to only allow either odd or even numbered IC numbers into the mall resulted in the complete decimation of foot traffic, rather than just a halving.

sections.label: Government role beyond internationalisation grants
sections.summary: Government can foster an expansionist mindset beyond internationalisation grants through wider recognition of ASEAN languages, required Southeast Asia exchanges and internships, regional trade show exposure and co-financing early career stints for PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Government can play an even greater role in fostering this expansionist mindset, beyond internationalisation grants.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It can do so with a wider recognition of ASEAN languages in the schooling system, incorporating exchanges and internships in Southeast Asia as a required component of Secondary and post-Secondary programmes, further enhancing the exposure of local firms in exhibitions at regional trade shows and co-financing early career stints for PMETs in other regional capitals.

sections.label: Plan B for fractured post-COVID world
sections.summary: A Plan B is needed in case the post-COVID-19 world is more fractured and insular, transitioning the economy by increasing SME contribution, with government helping beyond financing through productivity, regulatory flexibility and educational initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the globalising world, we need a Plan B to cater to the possibility that the post-COVID-19 world will be more fractured and insular.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We must transition our economy urgently and decisively by increasing the contribution of SMEs to our growth engine.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Government can help in this process with more than just financing, which is still our major focus.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It can do so with moves to improve the productivity of these businesses via enhance business skills and management training, exercising greater regulatory flexibility to foster a stronger risk-taking mindset and pushing additional educational and experiential initiatives that strengthen our regionalist worldview.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: My contention is that we need to accelerate and scale up these efforts.

sections.label: Digital ambassadors help elderly
sections.summary: Digital ambassadors help the elderly acquire digital skills at three levels, including video calls, e-payments and SafeEntry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: For example, our digital ambassadors have helped the elderly to take the first step towards digitalisation and help them acquire digital skills at three levels, so that they can keep in touch with their friends and relatives via video link, make e-payments at hawker centres and markets, and use SafeEntry in the SingPass mobile's visitors registration system to log in and out of wet markets.

sections.label: Woodgrove bank branches closed
sections.summary: Two local bank branches around Fuchun area closed or are renovating, so residents walk about 30 minutes for counter services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Recently, in Woodgrove, two local bank branches around Fuchun area were closed; one in mid-August and the other is undergoing renovation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Residents who need counter services have to walk about 30 minutes to go to the branches in the shopping mall.

sections.label: Bank staff and e-banking training
sections.summary: Trained frontline bank staff verify suspicious transactions, and banks can work with IMDA on e-banking training kiosks for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Frontline bank staff are specially trained to sense suspicious transactions and would verify with the customers repeatedly, so that they do not fall victim to fraud syndicates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Banks can work with IMDA to set up e-banking training kiosks at bank branches in the neighbourhood centres and digital transformation offices at CCs, to help seniors apply for online banking tokens, and teach them how to use online banking services with peace of mind.

sections.label: Semakau Landfill filling up faster
sections.summary: Semakau Landfill is filling faster than expected due to increased consumption, recyclables thrown as refuse, and reluctance to repair items.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: For the past few decades, we have relied on it for our waste disposal while being fortunate enough to be unaffected by any harmful toxins, awful smell and appearance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: However, Semakau Landfill has been filling up faster than expected, with our projections for reaching capacity changing for the worse.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: One, being a general increase in consumption by residents without sufficient implementation of the 3Rs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The second being that many recyclables are being disposed as general refuse, which in turn wastes landfill space and energy to incinerate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The other being that residents are largely reluctant to repair broken items which typically cause many faulty electrical and electronic appliances to be thrown away as rubbish instead of repairing it and extending its lifespan.

sections.label: Community Clubs Green Mark Platinum
sections.summary: Community Clubs, especially new or renovated ones, should endeavour to achieve BCA Green Mark Platinum certification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: For a start, our Community Clubs, CCs, especially those that are to be built or scheduled for renovation, should endeavour to achieve the BCA Green Mark "Platinum" certification.

sections.label: Resident refurbishes abandoned furniture
sections.summary: A Woodgrove resident refurbishes abandoned broken furniture as community gifts, which could encourage residents to reuse items and minimise waste.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: One of my residents in Woodgrove Zone 5, Christy, she shared with me her hobby of "Turning Trash to Treasure" – she would often go around the neighbourhood, sometimes to pick up and collect abandoned broken furniture.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: What she will do is, she will clean it up, she will refurbish it with a new coat of painting and transform it into fashionable new furniture as gifts for the community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I believe that introducing such concepts can raise awareness and encourage more residents to conserve resources by sharing and reusing pre-loved items to minimise waste generation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Just like the COVID-19 pandemic, climate change is a very challenging global issue that cannot be resolved overnight.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: That said, I am confident that together, we will overcome these challenges and emerge stronger as a nation.

sections.label: Couples delaying children due to COVID-19
sections.summary: A June NPTD and MSF survey found three in 10 Singaporean couples planned to delay having a child because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In a NPTD and MSF Survey in June, three in 10 Singaporean couples said that they were planning to delay having a child due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: Baby Support Grant and fertility decline
sections.summary: Fertility declines with age, so the Baby Support Grant was created to encourage couples not to postpone parenthood plans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We are also concerned because we recognise that fertility declines with age and chances of conception are much higher when couples start earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Hence, we developed the idea of the Baby Support Grant to augment the existing Baby Bonus Cash Gift to provide extra support for parents who wish to have a child, so that they will not postpone their parenthood plans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Given the policy intent to encourage more couples to proceed with their parenthood plans, we could have taken a very strict approach and if you take a strict approach, it would mean that the start date should be nine months after the date of announcement, which would actually be July 2021.

sections.label: Baby Support Grant start date October 2020
sections.summary: Despite a tight fiscal situation, Budget was set aside and the grant was made effective from 1 October 2020, the month of announcement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: While the Government's fiscal situation is tight, due to the support given to Singaporeans and businesses throughout the year, we were able to set aside some Budget this year, to provide additional support to more Singaporean parents starting as soon as we could.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Hence, we decided to make it effective from the month of announcement, that is, 1 October 2020.

sections.label: Petitions for other grant dates
sections.summary: Some suggested 1 January 2020, when the pandemic started, while another petition asked the grant to cover children one year and below on 1 October.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Many have suggested that it should be with effect from 1 January 2020 as that was when the pandemic started and indeed there is a petition supporting this date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: But, on the other hand, there is another petition asking for the grant to cover all children who are one year and below on 1 October of this year.

sections.label: October date kept, premature babies exception
sections.summary: The October commencement date is maintained, but appeals are acceded to for babies born before 1 October 2020 whose certified EDD was on or after that date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Each group has reasons for the dates proposed and looking at it from their perspective, these reasons are all valid, but we can only choose one date and whichever date we choose, there will be groups who are not covered.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We chose October as the commencement date for the reasons mentioned earlier and we seek your understanding, that is why we are maintaining this date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: But we will, however, accede to appeals for the Baby Support Grant from a specific group of parents – those whose babies were born before 1 October 2020, but whose certified Estimated Delivery Date, or EDD, was on or after 1 October 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In other words, born prematurely although the EDD was 1 October 2020 onwards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The National Population and Talent Division will provide more information to parents on how they can do so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: That said, it is important to understand where the parents who have asked for an earlier date are coming from.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: So, I would like to reassure them and Members, that even without the Baby Support Grant, there is still substantial Government support for these parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: While the extra Baby Support Grant is for babies born from 1 October 2020, parents whose babies were born before 1 October 2020 will receive, and in some cases, have already received cash and cash-like benefits, which were last enhanced in 2015 and 2016.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: They would have received, for example: (a) between $8,000 and $10,000 in the Baby Bonus Cash Gift; (b) $3,000 First Step Grant, deposited into the Child Development Account or the CDA, without parents having to first save into the CDA; (c) between $3,000 and $15,000 in Government co-savings for the CDA; and (d) a $4,000 grant which is deposited into the Medisave account that is open for every newborn, that is the Medisave Grant for Newborns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, the total cash and cash-like support that parents can receive ranges from $18,000 for their first child to $32,000 for their fifth and subsequent children, even without the Baby Support Grant.

sections.label: Additional Subsidy income ceiling raised
sections.summary: Since 1 January 2020, the household income ceiling for the Additional Subsidy was raised from $7,500 to $12,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Since 1 January 2020, the household income ceiling for the Additional Subsidy has been raised from $7,500 per month to $12,000 per month.

sections.label: Infant and childcare subsidy amounts
sections.summary: After enhanced subsidies, families can receive up to $1,310 monthly for infant care or up to $767 monthly for childcare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Today, after the enhanced subsidies, families can receive up to $1,310 each month in infant care subsidies or up to $767 each month in childcare subsidies.

sections.label: Free vaccinations and screenings
sections.summary: From 1 November 2020, all Singaporean children can receive free national schedule vaccinations and developmental screenings at Polyclinics and CHAS GPs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: From 1 November 2020, that means next month, all Singaporean children – and this applies to all Singaporean children today regardless of when they were born – can also receive free childhood vaccinations on the national schedule and developmental screenings, at all Polyclinics and Community Health Assist Scheme General Practitioners or CHAS GPs.

sections.label: Ineligibility answer
sections.summary: The passage states that they would not be eligible for it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The answer is that they would not be eligible for it.

sections.label: Benefits regardless of parents' marital status
sections.summary: Government benefits supporting children's growth are given to all Singaporean children regardless of parents' marital status, including subsidies, MediSave Grant, MediShield Life, leave, levy concession, education and healthcare subsidies, and social assistance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, it is not quite consistent to extend it to singles in this context.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: However, I would like to assure all that Government benefits that support the growth and development of children are given to all Singaporean children, regardless of the marital status of their parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, benefits that are available to all parents to support them in their care-giving responsibilities would include childcare and infant care subsidies, the MediSave Grant for newborns, MediShield Life coverage from birth, infant care and childcare leave, the Foreign Domestic Worker Levy concession and, in addition to the above, every Singaporean child will benefit from education and healthcare subsidies and has access to social assistance, regardless of their parents' marital status.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In 2016 and 2017, we further extended support to unwed parents, including the Government-Paid Maternity Leave and the Child Development Account which includes the CDA First Step, that is, the $3,000 I mentioned earlier, and the matched co-savings from the Government.

sections.label: Support for families with babies
sections.summary: The Government understands difficulties families with babies and young children face and seeks understanding about the Baby Support Grant start date.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We do understand the difficulties that families, especially those with babies and young children, face during this period, and have implemented measures like the one I described earlier.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We will continue to support families during these extraordinary times and I seek Members’ and fellow Singaporeans’ understanding about the start date for the Baby Support Grant, which is one additional measure among many.

sections.label: Baby Support Grant policy intent
sections.summary: The scheme aims to encourage those delaying parenthood plans, and low-income parents with children from 1 October onwards will get the Baby Support Grant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I think the approach that we would take is this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This particular scheme has a very specific policy intent, which is to encourage those who are delaying to proceed with their parenthood plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: If they are low income and they have children from 1 October onwards, they will get the Baby Support Grant.

sections.label: Help for low-income parents
sections.summary: Assurance that low-income parents with financial difficulties who had a child before 1 October will be helped through schemes like ComCare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The SSOs were set up for this purpose, ComCare was put in place for this purpose and there are many different schemes which are aimed at that.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, the assurance that we can give is that if you are low income and you have had your child before 1 October and you have financial difficulties, we will help you.

sections.label: Baby Support Grant for unwed parents
sections.summary: A hope that the Government reconsiders not giving the Baby Support Grant to single unwed parents, noting their median salary is about $600 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, I really hope the Government could reconsider not providing the Baby Support Grant to the single unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We also have to bear in mind that the median salary of a single unwed parent under 35 years old is about $600 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, the $3,000 is actually about five months of their salary and it could really provide a lifeline for them during this pandemic.

sections.label: Levy proportional to EP salary
sections.summary: A levy proportional to the salary of the EP holder is fair and can be justified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: A levy proportional to the salary of the EP holder is fair and can be justified.

sections.label: Support for Singaporean workers
sections.summary: Suggestions to balance measures with foreign PMET quotas, extend the COVID-19 Support Grant, and enhance WIS payouts for the lowest income group.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: This is a group of Singaporeans whom I am especially concerned about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: It would be good to balance these measures with quotas for foreign PMETs to encourage and incentivise companies to employ Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: Could the JGI be a long-term policy coupled with support for employers to provide permanent upgrading and upskilling of Singaporean workers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: May we extend the COVID-19 Support Grant or CSG to those who were not eligible for the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme or SIRS?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: Can we also enhance the WIS payout for lowest 25% income group with more payment for the lowest tier, with up to 50% more grants to supplement their income?

sections.label: Survey on working from home
sections.summary: In a May survey of 9,000 respondents across 90 companies, 90% said they wanted to continue working from home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In a survey of 9,000 respondents across night 90 companies conducted this May, 90% of respondents said they wanted to continue working from home.

sections.label: Fathers' involvement during circuit breaker
sections.summary: A Focus on the Family Singapore survey of nearly 2,500 fathers found 70% became more involved with their families during the circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A survey conducted by Focus on the Family Singapore this year found that out of nearly 2,500 fathers, 70% became more involved with their families during the circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Of this group, more than 80% said they connected better with their kids.

sections.label: Ctrip work from home productivity
sections.summary: A US National Bureau of Economic Research study found Ctrip employees were 13% more productive working from home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A study again by the US National Bureau of Economic Research found that employees of China's largest travel agency, Ctrip, were 13% more productive while working from home.

sections.label: Ctrip attrition rate halved
sections.summary: Ctrip halved its employee attrition rate with a work from home policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Ctrip, the Chinese travel agency I mentioned previously, halved their attrition rate of their employees, with a work from home policy.

sections.label: Singapore score below Southeast Asia
sections.summary: Singapore scored 61.1% in 2019, below Vietnam, Cambodia and Lao PDR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On that, Singapore scored 61.1% in 2019, far below other countries in Southeast Asia, such as Vietnam at 72.5%; Cambodia at 75.2% and Lao PDR at 76.8%.

sections.label: Closing gap adds GDP
sections.summary: The study estimates closing this gap could add over $26 billion to Singapore's GDP by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The study estimates that if we close this gap, more than $26 billion could be added to the Singapore's GDP by 2025.

sections.label: UK work from home right
sections.summary: The UK gives all workers the right to request work from home, which employers can reject only for certain business reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The UK has done what I am calling for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It provides the right for all workers to request for work from home, which employers can reject only based on certain business reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A study conducted in 2018 found that less than 5% of UK workers who worked from home or used staggered hours experience negative consequences due to their working arrangement.

sections.label: Minister Lawrence work from home normal
sections.summary: Minister Lawrence said work from home must be embraced as a new normal even after circuit breaker ends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Minister Lawrence has said that working from home must be embraced as a new normal even after circuit breaker ends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We are now at a 50% work from home policy and I urge the Government not to reduce this any further, but instead take a step forward and ensure that work from home truly becomes a new normal.

sections.label: Lowest percentile wage growth
sections.summary: Wages of workers at the lowest 20th percentile rose 24% in real terms over five years and 39% over ten years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The wages of workers at the lowest 20th percentile have increased by 24% in real terms in the last five years and by 39% over the last 10 years.

sections.label: Gini coefficient after transfers
sections.summary: The Gini coefficient using OECD methodology fell to 0.35 in 2019 after accounting for Government transfers such as Workfare Income Supplement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Gini coefficient calculated using the widely used OECD methodology, fell to 0.35 in 2019 after accounting for Government transfers such as Workfare Income Supplement.

sections.label: PWM lifted workers' wages
sections.summary: The PWM lifted the wages of close to 80,000 cleaners, security officers and landscape workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The PWM lifted the wages of close to 80,000 cleaners, security officers and landscape workers.

sections.label: Extending PWM to all sectors
sections.summary: The Government committed to working with tripartite partners to extend the PWM to all sectors appropriately to each sector's unique conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Government has committed to working with its tripartite partners to extend the PWM to all sectors in a manner that is appropriate to each and every sector's unique conditions.

sections.label: Workers earning under $1,300
sections.summary: With Workfare and employer's CPF contribution included, only about 56,000 across various job roles earn less than $1,300.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: With Workfare and employer's CPF contribution included, only about 56,000 across a variety of job roles earn less than $1,300.

sections.label: Workers' Party minimum wage call
sections.summary: The Workers' Party called for a $1,300 monthly Minimum Wage across all sectors as a quick way to cover everyone else.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party have called for a Minimum Wage of $1,300 a month to be applied across all sectors, as a quick way to cover everyone else.

sections.label: Town Council cleaner starting salary
sections.summary: The passage states Town Council cleaners' PWM starting salary is $1,442, higher than the Workers' Party's proposed $1,300 minimum wage.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: For example, the starting salary for a cleaner in Town Councils today under the mandatory PWM is already $1,442.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: With overtime pay, Workfare Income Supplement and Annual Wage Supplement or bonuses, this would be much higher than the $1,300 a month that the Workers' Party proposes as a minimum wage.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Indeed, because of the mandatory PWM, the Workers' Party Town Councils' cleaners are being paid based on the PWM and not based on their Minimum Wage!

sections.label: Blanket minimum wage politicisation risk
sections.summary: The passage states a second risk of a single blanket Minimum Wage is the inevitable politicisation of wage setting.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The second risk – with a single blanket Minimum Wage is the inevitable politicisation of wage setting.

sections.label: NTUC tripartite workgroup on PWM
sections.summary: NTUC will continue talks via the new tripartite Workgroup on expanding PWM and welcomes the PWM Mark introduced by Minister Josephine Teo.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: NTUC will continue our conversations with our tripartite partners via the newly convened tripartite Workgroup on expanding PWM, to ensure that we take into account the concerns of all our stakeholders for a sustainable implementation of the PWMs, even as we work collectively to help ourselves to get out of this economic recession.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In the interim, the PWM Mark that was recently introduced by Minister Josephine Teo in Parliament as a potential means of recognising firms that voluntarily pay progressive wages, is something that we welcome.

sections.label: Waste management PWM and sectoral benchmark
sections.summary: NTUC proposed a Tripartite Cluster for Waste Management to introduce a PWM, and suggests studying a sectoral wage benchmark.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Beyond the lift and escalator PWM becoming mandatory in 2022, NTUC had also submitted a proposal to the Government to form a Tripartite Cluster for the Waste Management Industry to introduce a PWM focusing on the waste collection sub- sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We look forward to the Government’s strong support and will work closely with our tripartite partners to bring about better wages, welfare and work prospects for the low-wage workers in this sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In expanding the PWM, we should also consider studying other approaches to complement the existing PWM efforts, such as setting a sectoral wage benchmark as a first step for companies in sectors where there are currently no regulatory levers to mandate a PWM.

sections.label: Minimum Wage for below $1,300
sections.summary: The passage states the proposal concerns Singaporeans earning below the $1,300 mark, and there is no reason for concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I would like to start with, actually, what I felt was a very powerful line from the Senior Minister of State, which was he is not so much concerned at our proposal of a Minimum Wage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And indeed, there is no reason to be very concerned about it because what we are talking about is those Singaporeans who earn below the $1,300 mark.

sections.label: Figures for below $1,300 workers
sections.summary: The passage asks what happens to those below the $1,300 floor, citing 100,000 workers, a quarter self-employed, 56,000 not full-time, 32,000 full-time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And for those who are significantly below the $1,300 floor, what will happen to them?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And that is precisely my question for the numbers that the Senior Minister of State had shared – about the 100,000, a quarter of them self-employed; 56,000 not full-time workers, if I remember correctly, and 32,000 are full-time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I think this is the first time the Government has shared these figures.

sections.label: Lift company cost increase
sections.summary: For one lift company, costs are going up by 47%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For one lift company, costs are going up by 47%.

sections.label: Minimum Wage excludes foreign domestic workers
sections.summary: The proposed Minimum Wage does not include foreign domestic workers at this point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minimum Wage we are proposing does not include foreign domestic workers at this point.

sections.label: 1.7% of workforce
sections.summary: The figure stated is 1.7% of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Workforce – I beg your pardon. 1.7% of the workforce.

sections.label: PWM applies to Singaporean workers
sections.summary: The PWM as it stands today applies only to the Singaporean local workforce, so wage increases benefit only Singapore workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The good news of course is that the PWM, as it stands today, applies only to Singaporean local workforce, Singaporean workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, wage increases for PWM only benefits Singapore workers.

sections.label: 1.7% local workforce data
sections.summary: The data of 1.7% of the local workforce is not very clean because it includes people across different job roles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The data, 1.7% percent of the local workforce, it is not a very clean data because it includes a whole group of people across different job roles.

sections.label: Businesses absorb or pass on costs
sections.summary: Businesses either absorb the cost or rationalise passing it to consumers, and Mr Singh is prepared to raise S&CC charges to justify higher wage cost when the mandatory PWM for lift and escalator sectors is pushed up.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Where the businesses are prepared to absorb the cost; if not, they have a way to rationalise how to pass the cost on to the consumers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I am glad to hear that Mr Singh is prepared to also raise the S&CC charges to justify for higher wage cost when we eventually push up the mandatory PWM for the lift and escalator sectors, to make sure that our brothers and sisters in this sector get get paid a fair wage.

sections.label: Justifying $1,300 minimum wage
sections.summary: The speaker says a clear justification was made for why $1,300 is a justifiable number.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: So, that leaves us with discussing why, what is too high?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: And again, I think we made a clear justification on why we believe that $1,300 is a justifiable number.

sections.label: Independent wage board proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes an independent wage board of academics, Labour Movement and employer representatives to set a number without politicisation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Which is why, one way forward is to ensure that we have an independent wage board comprised of academics as well as representatives from both the Labour Movement as well as employers to come up with a number so that is not politicised.

sections.label: Profiteering and wage increases
sections.summary: The speaker says paying workers enough need not hurt small businesses and asks how tripartite partners assess profiteering in a sector.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: So, when we pay our workers enough, it need not be the case that our small businesses end up suffering as a result.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I believe Senior Minister of State has not answered my question with regard to how the tripartite partners assess in a particular sector whether profiteering is taking place on the back of what ought to be wage increases for our Singaporean workers.

sections.label: Companies pricing in future increases
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether it is legitimately correct for some companies to already price in future increases today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: My point is, this is in the future, but some of these companies are already pricing it in today and is that legitimately correct for them to do so?

sections.label: Small number affected by minimum wage
sections.summary: The Senior Minister of State said the number of people affected by a $1,300 monthly minimum wage could be very small.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State did say that the number of people who will be affected by a minimum wage of $1,300 per month could actually be very small.

sections.label: Helping lower wage workers
sections.summary: The speaker says wage is only one aspect of helping lower wage workers, citing Workfare top-ups without employer hoops or heavy lifting.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: How do we help the lower wage workers, maybe the 1.7% that we spoke about?

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I think when we look at this, wage is only one aspect of helping a lower wage worker.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Today, with Workfare, we already top up the wages and that is one way of helping them without having to make employers jump through the hoops, without having to make disadvantaged workers that have to do a lot of heavy lifting to get to the Minimum Wage, for example.

sections.label: Minimum Wage and PWM sectors
sections.summary: The Workers' Party would argue that a $1,300 Minimum Wage for the lowest paying PWM sector is fine if other sectors pay more.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: What I believe that the Workers’ Party would argue is that if you can establish that the Minimum Wage for the lowest paying sector within the PWM is at least $1,300, it is absolutely fine if the other sectors were willing to pay more than that $1,300, for that particular lowest pay sector.

sections.label: Wages, productivity and competitiveness
sections.summary: The speaker says the 32,000 people do not feel taken care of, and higher wages must be coupled with higher productivity for businesses to stay competitive.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Even if it is 32,000 people, I do not think that any of these 32,000 people feel that they are being taken care of.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Businesses need to stay competitive and avoid passing all costs to consumers to stay competitive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, an increased wage has to be coupled with an increase in productivity.

sections.label: Minimum Wage versus skills ladder
sections.summary: The speaker says a Minimum Wage is an unconnected fluctuating number, while the PWM ties a skills ladder to rising wages.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: If we stipulate a Minimum Wage or whatever wage there is, but the employer feels that this is not worth paying for, or if you set the wage too high, he will say, “Well, with this money, I might as well buy a machine to do this job.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Because I will amortise this machine over one year, two years, and my return is immeasurable, beyond the ROI".

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This worker will never get the job if he is priced too high.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: On the other hand, if you fix the rate too low, but yet the worker does not have the skills to do the job, no matter how low you price the Minimum Wage, I would not employ the person anyway because there is no skills to it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, that is why in the PWM construct, it is not just a wage ladder – rising wages across a spectrum, but actually, there is a skills ladder that is tied to it so that as the employee gets the skills that justify the productivity, the work output and the work delivery, the wages commensurate with their skills will be paid to the employee.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The problem with a Minimum Wage is that it is not connected to any skills ladder.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: It is a number, and the employer then has to decide if the employee makes the mark or is too costly for him, and that number can fluctuate.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme wage subsidies
sections.summary: Businesses received Jobs Support Scheme wage subsidies of 75% to retain workers, extended until next March.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: For example, we have provided extensive support to businesses through the Jobs Support Scheme, with wage subsidies of 75% to help businesses retain workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister has announced that this support will be extended until next March.

sections.label: Jobs Growth Incentive hiring support
sections.summary: Eligible employers receive up to 25% of the first $5,000 of gross monthly wages for new local hires below 40, doubled for mature hires and PwDs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Eligible employers will receive up to 25% of the first $5,000 of gross monthly wages, or $15,000 for up to 12 months, for new local hires aged below 40.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: For each new mature local hire aged 40 and above and for all persons with disabilities or PwDs, Government support is doubled to 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Thus far, we have committed $1 billion to this initiative, and we encourage more firms to make use of the JGI to expand hiring.

sections.label: Retrenched workers re-entering employment
sections.summary: About 39% of workers retrenched in the first quarter of 2020 had re-entered employment by June 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Around 39% of workers retrenched in the first quarter of 2020 had re-entered employment by June 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Of these, seven in 10 re-entered employment within a month of being retrenched and five in 10 possessed transferrable skills that enabled them to switch to a different industry.

sections.label: Support for mature jobseekers
sections.summary: The JGI gives higher salary support for new mature local hires and boosted support for workers aged 40 and above in career conversion programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We are aware and recognise the challenges this group of jobseekers face.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: I have already mentioned that the JGI will provide higher salary support for new mature local hires – double that, compared to non-mature hires.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This aims to support mid-career jobseekers in reskilling for new occupations in sectors with good long-term prospects.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We have also boosted the salary support for all workers aged 40 and above who are enrolled in career conversion programmes, in particular, for non-PMETs, from 70% to 90%.

sections.label: Work Permit and S Pass quotas
sections.summary: Services and S Pass quotas were cut in 2020 and will be further reduced in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: At the Work Permit and S Pass level, we cut the services quota from 40% to 38% and the S Pass quota from 15% to 13% in 2020, and this will be further reduced to 35% and 10% respectively in 2021, that is, next year.

sections.label: Penalties for fair consideration infringements
sections.summary: This year, 90 employers had work pass privileges suspended for infringements under the FCF.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We also regularly take employers to task for pre-selecting foreign candidates and disregarding qualified local candidates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This year alone, 90 employers have had their work pass privileges suspended because of infringements under the FCF.

sections.label: Income growth under PWM
sections.summary: In the three PWM sectors, real incomes rose about 30%, and 10th percentile full-time resident worker incomes rose 50% over the last decade.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In the three sectors where the PWM has been implemented, real incomes have increased by around 30% in recent years, outstripping the 21% of real income growth at the median across all sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The incomes of our 10th percentile full-time resident workers today, currently stands at $1,517.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: One decade ago, the incomes of this percentile of workers was at $1,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This amounts to a 50% increase over the last decade.

sections.label: Workfare and training support
sections.summary: Workfare tops up low-wage workers' income by up to 30% and provides targeted training support for better employment outcomes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Our sense of solidarity with our low-wage workers also goes beyond wages.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We have taken a careful and practical approach to implement a holistic suite of measures: Workfare that tops up the income of low-wage workers by up to 30% and provides targeted training support that supports better employment outcomes.

sections.label: SIRS disbursements and recipients
sections.summary: SIRS has disbursed over $1.1 billion in two tranches, is expected to cost $2 billion in total, and about 195,000 individuals have received support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In the first two tranches of SIRS, we have disbursed over $1.1 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: With the third and final tranches, SIRS is expected to cost $2 billion in total, almost double the original $1.2 billion set aside.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Altogether, about 195,000 individuals have received support under SIRS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: About two in three unique applications have been approved.

sections.label: Industry support packages as lifelines
sections.summary: JSS, SIRS, CSG and industry grants provided lifelines for Singaporeans and companies and should continue as a supportive foundation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: JSS, SIRS, CSG, various industry support packages, different industry grants – they have all provided valuable lifelines for Singaporeans and Singaporean companies to pull them out of the river of crocodiles and get them out from a very difficult period, and would be important to continue to be that supportive foundation that Singaporeans can reply on moving forward.

sections.label: COVID-19 impact on sports and arts
sections.summary: COVID-19 affected sports and fitness workers and businesses, and the speaker asks what more can be done mid-to-long-term for arts, culture, sports and fitness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Besides that, COVID-19 has also had an impact on those who are in the sports and fitness industries, regardless of whether they are hired employees, freelance coaches or instructors or owners of sports and fitness related businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is thus heartening to note that some activities such as the Singapore Premier League or SPL will be resuming soon, this weekend, if I am not mistaken, and the Government has managed to relax the guidelines and constraints around sporting activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am aware that my Parliamentary colleagues, Members of Parliament, Ms Carrie Tan and Minister of State, Ms Low Yen Ling had a good debate about safeguarding the livelihood of our Arts & Culture professionals in Parliament last week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And it is heartening to know that MCCY is taking steps in this direction, especially in terms of helping to support our Arts & Culture freelance performers and also in terms of creating professional opportunities or projects that our performers can work on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What I would like the Government to consider is what more can be done, in the mid-to long-term to ensure that we are better to support the Arts & Culture and Sports & Fitness industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It would be good, in Arts & Culture for example, if the MCCY could see how they could partner with the MOE to bring arts and culture more into the curriculum and integrate arts and culture into our schools' curriculum – not just in terms of subjects being taught by MOE such as music, art or drama which are sometimes taught in formal context by trained MOE teachers, but by ensuring that all students are exposed to the various arts at all levels of the curriculum.

sections.label: Embedding sports, arts and culture
sections.summary: Quoting the Prime Minister on bread and the finer things in life, the speaker hopes Government will further embed sports, arts and culture in community and people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I do not know if Prime Minister remembers this or not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It was in 2015, I believe, Prime Minister or 2014 and I quote, "Creating jobs, upgrading workers, making Singapore a more attractive place to work – these are all important things in life." And I agree. "You have to put bread on the table.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But 'Man does not live by bread alone'.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We do wish for the finer things in life, to appreciate beauty and love, and something uplifting for the spirit." Mr Speaker, Sir, sports, arts, culture, these are indeed uplifting for the spirit and I believe that it is about getting that balance right that even as we extend support to these industries, I would hope that the Government can go one step further to take this opportunity to further embed sports, arts and culture not just in the fabric of our community, but in the psyche and the soul of our people as well.

sections.label: Workers' Party minimum wage proposal
sections.summary: The speaker says assessment must be based on totality of results and notes the Workers' Party proposes a minimum wage of $1,300.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Rather, we have to base it on the totality of the results and I think if you look at the totality of the results, you will see that a very low Minimum Wage – what the Workers' Party is proposing is a minimum wage of $1,300.

sections.label: Contested studies and wage growth
sections.summary: The speaker says studies are hotly contested and cites 30% wage growth for low-wage workers in the last five years without Minimum Wage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: It is about this, the studies being hotly contested and the academia, I think you can throw studies to each other and we can never come to conclusive position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: So, I think this is about how we have applied, how we have also shown how wages have grown and I have shared the examples earlier, where our low-wage workers have seen wage growth – 30% in the last five years without Minimum Wage.

sections.label: Wage growth at 10th percentile
sections.summary: At the 10th percentile, wages rose from $1,000 ten years ago to $1,500-plus now, a 50% growth for the lowest income threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: At the 10th percentile, it was $1,000 10 years ago; it is now $1,500-plus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We have seen a 50% wage growth in the last 10 years for the lowest income threshold.

sections.label: Tripartite Workgroup for Low-wage Workers
sections.summary: The Government set up the Tripartite Workgroup for Low-wage Workers to find ways to uplift low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Yes, there will be some but this is an area we have to look at and that is why the Government is serious.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We have put in the Tripartite Workgroup for Low-wage Workers specifically to see how we can do better in uplifting our low-wage workers.

sections.label: Minimum Wage and Living Wage proposals
sections.summary: The Workers' Party proposes a Minimum Wage and the PSP favours something similar called a Living Wage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: One is that do you not think that the Minimum Wage that Workers' Party is proposing and PSP is also in favour of something similar called Living Wage.

sections.label: Bold idea amid uncertainty
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a bold idea should be implemented during this uncertain period and says fears of losing competitiveness or jobs may be overblown.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Do you have a fresh perspective to add?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, I am asking do you not think that this can be a bold idea to implement during this period of very uncertainty and we have to emerge from the crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Second question is that I think the point about there being a danger of losing competitiveness or losing jobs may be a bit overblown.

sections.label: COVID-19 event and group limits
sections.summary: Fighting COVID-19 required suspending large-scale events and limiting group sizes to five.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Yet, this is precisely what we cannot now do, as we continue to fight against COVID-19, to keep Singaporeans safe and to keep the virus at bay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We have had to suspend large-scale events and limit group sizes to five.

sections.label: Rental waivers and venue subsidies
sections.summary: Rental waivers were provided to tenants in SportSG facilities and arts venues, and venue hire subsidies for cultural institution users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To help them manage overheads, we have provided rental waivers to tenants in SportSG facilities and arts venues, as well as venue hire subsidies for users of our cultural institutions.

sections.label: Arts and Culture Resilience package
sections.summary: The Arts and Culture Resilience package generated over 10,000 work and training opportunities, including almost 4,000 for freelancers, and supported close to 1,200 digitalisation projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Arts and Culture Resilience (ACR) package has generated over 10,000 work and training opportunities, of which almost 4,000 alone were for freelancers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It has also supported close to 1,200 digitalisation projects and programmes by local artists and organisations.

sections.label: KpopX instructor virtual classes
sections.summary: Jasmine Wong, a certified KpopX fitness instructor, has conducted 85 virtual classes on the Circle since April.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Jasmine Wong, a certified KpopX fitness instructor, has conducted 85 virtual classes on the Circle since April.

sections.label: ACRP Operating Grant for arts organisations
sections.summary: Eligible arts and culture organisations will receive a one-off ACRP Operating Grant of $75,000 or $50,000, depending on organisation size, expected to benefit over 300 organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Eligible arts and culture organisations will receive a one-off ACRP Operating Grant of either $75,000 or $50,000 which they can use to defray their operating costs, and the amount depends on the size of their organisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Pay it forward, like what Objectifs and JASS have done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This grant is expected to benefit over 300 organisations and more information will be made available by NAC in end-October and we will also reach out directly to eligible organisations to tell them about this and to assist them in their application.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: With this grant, we expect to fully utilise the $55 million set aside for the ACRP by the end of FY2020.

sections.label: Sports Resilience Package operating grant
sections.summary: The SRP will provide eligible businesses an operating grant covering up to 25% of operating expenses, capped at $15,000 monthly, for six months from October 2020 to March 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
