sentences.text: With this in mind, the Sports Resilience Package (SRP) will provide eligible businesses with an operating grant to cover up to 25% of their total operating expenses, capped at $15,000 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And this will last for six months, beginning from October 2020 right through to March 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We hope to be able to support up to 150 sports businesses with this operating grant, helping operators who do not currently receive Government funding.

sections.label: SRP funding for Blended initiative
sections.summary: Under the SRP, $5 million will be provided to expand the existing Blended initiative to include eligible private academies and clubs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Under the SRP, we will provide $5 million to help expand the existing Blended initiative to include eligible private academies and clubs as well.

sections.label: SRP support for coaches
sections.summary: Under the SRP, $2.5 million is set aside for a training allowance for NROC coaches and a structured mentorship programme for selected coaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To support them, we have set aside $2.5 million under the SRP for two initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: First, coaches who are registered under the National Registry of Coaches or NROC can receive a training allowance of $10 per hour when they take up courses run by CoachSG, and this is when you take it up beyond the Continuing Coach Education courses that they take.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Second, CoachSG will select 50 to 80 pairs of Level 2 and Level 3 NROC-registered coaches to participate in its structured mentorship programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To encourage this, participants will be provided between $400 and $600 per month to sign up for this mentorship programme.

sections.label: Worship limits and live music pilots
sections.summary: All ROs may conduct congregational and worship activities for up to 100 persons since 3 October 2020, and two pilots have commenced on higher limits and live music.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Following a successful pilot of the increase in worship limits to 100 persons, all ROs have been allowed to conduct congregational and worship activities/services for up to 100 persons – with the necessary safe management measures in place – that has been the case since 3 October 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Many have shared that singing and live music are integral to the way they practice their faith.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, we have commenced two separate pilots, in selected ROs – one to allow up to 250 persons at a time for worship services; and another a pilot to resume live music for worship services across different faith groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We will see how that goes, study them, take on the lessons to be learnt, and consider whether we can extend the higher worship limits and live music subsequently to all other ROs and religious activities.

sections.label: Ambition for Singaporean Arts
sections.summary: The question asks how far Singapore sets its sights for the arts sector and what its international ambition is.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: My question to the Minister is how far are we as a country setting our sights for the future of our Singaporean Arts for the sector?

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: Do we have and what is our ambition for Singaporean Arts internationally if there is even one at this moment?

sections.label: Culture Academy Mentioned
sections.summary: Ms Tan might know that a Culture Academy exists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Ms Tan might know that we have a Culture Academy.

sections.label: Growing Singapore Arts Sector
sections.summary: Many cultural institutions and arts people show sector growth, and the speaker shares a passion to make Singapore art global.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The fact that we have so many different cultural institutions and we had a room full of people from the different types of arts from visual, to theatre, to performing, to music, says a lot about how we have grown that sector over the past years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But, we are never content with where we are and I share Ms Tan's passion to make Singapore art not just local but also global, to blend what we want to do here with our unique Singaporean heritage and identity, with what we can deliver on the world stage.

sections.label: Government Economic Support Spending
sections.summary: Over $31 billion, almost 7% of GDP, was injected to save jobs and businesses, plus over $4 billion in payouts and $6 billion for the GST Voucher Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: More than $31 billion in total, or almost 7% of GDP, directly injected by the Government into our economy to save jobs, keep viable businesses afloat and put a floor beneath an unprecedented economic contraction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Government also estimates that it would spend more than $4 billion in Care and Support cash payouts, GST vouchers, service and conservancy charges rebates, utilities credits and Passion Card top-ups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: More extraordinarily, the Government has maintained its initial commitment of $6 billion in the Unity Budget for the GST Voucher Fund.

sections.label: Endowment and Trust Fund Commitments
sections.summary: The Government maintained Unity Budget commitments: $5 billion for coastal protection, $2 billion each for research and skills, and almost $1 billion for ElderCare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: On the contrary, the Government is doing the responsible thing, by recognising the GST Voucher scheme for what it is, a permanent commitment by the Government to help Singaporeans and keep GST progressive for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And staying the course we are, in other areas as well, the Government has maintained its initial commitment in the Unity Budget for all other sums, for various endowment and trust funds: $5 billion to the Coastal and Flood Protection Fund, for our 100-year defence plan against rising sea levels; $2 billion to the National Research Fund, $2 billion to the Skills Development Fund and almost $1 billion to the ElderCare Fund, to save up for our future healthcare needs.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills Openings
sections.summary: Almost 120,000 openings were curated and over 33,000 jobseekers placed, with around 84,000 openings still unfilled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: As of end August, almost 120,000 openings have been curated under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package and more than 33,000 jobseekers have been placed into these openings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: While this has been encouraging progress, it remains that around 84,000 openings are as yet unfilled.

sections.label: Resourcing e2i and WSG
sections.summary: The speaker proposes resourcing e2i and WSG beyond current levels to enable decisive outcomes for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: To this end, I propose that we resource e2i and WSG decisively beyond today's levels to enable decisive outcomes for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Deferred development expenditure total
sections.summary: The total amount of deferred development expenditure is almost $7 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: The total amount of deferred development expenditure is almost $7 billion.

sections.label: Outlook for key investments
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Government to clarify the overall outlook for key investments and whether the investment timeline will be pushed out or investment cut back.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: At the same time, I hope the Government could clarify our overall outlook for these key investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Certainly, we should not expect a catch-up in deferred capital expenditure in the next few years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And so, I echo the hon Member Mr Murali Pillai's question and ask: are we looking to push out the investment timeline, or are we expecting to cut back on our overall level of investment?

sections.label: COVID-19 Support Grant wage subsidies
sections.summary: The speaker suggests wage subsidies based on degree of income loss, noting the COVID-19 Support Grant requires at least 30% income reduction for three consecutive months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: First, one of the current conditions for the COVID-19 Support Grant is a reduction of at least 30% in income for three consecutive months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I suggest that the Government provide wage subsidies based on the degree of income loss of the applicants so that more Singaporeans can receive appropriate assistance to avoid the current cliff effect.

sections.label: Resources committed under four Budgets
sections.summary: Resources committed under the four Budgets amounted to about $100 billion, on top of other measures such as special relief measures for debtors and tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As the hon Member Mr Xie mentioned just now, the resources committed under the four Budgets are significant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It amounted to about $100 billion and this is on top of the other measures, such as special relief measures for debtors and tenants.

sections.label: Stimulus package share of GDP
sections.summary: The stimulus package endorsed in Parliament amounted to 21% of the GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The stimulus package that we have endorsed in Parliament here amounted to 21% of the GDP.

sections.label: Budget impact on jobs
sections.summary: Four Budgets are estimated to prevent economic contraction and save about 155,000 jobs over two years, while money must be spent well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: It is also the positive impact on the lives and livelihoods in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: It is worth restating what Deputy Prime Minister had said in his Statement that "The four Budgets are estimated to prevent the economy from contracting by 5.6% of GDP this year and 4.8 % next year." Furthermore, he said that "an estimated 155,000 jobs are likely to be saved in these two years too." At the same time, we owe a duty to spend the money well.

sections.label: MAS programme extension
sections.summary: MAS decided to extend a programme originally scheduled to finish in December 2020 to 30 June 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: I filed a Parliamentary Question or PQ on this earlier this month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: I had suggested an extension of the programme in my PQ and I am glad to note that MAS has decided to extend this programme which is originally scheduled to finish in December 2020 to 30 June 2021.

sections.label: Debt conversions under programme
sections.summary: Under the programme, financial institutions granted over 8,100 conversions amounting to $200 million of personal unsecured debt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In his reply to my PQ, the hon Senior Minister, Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam, informed that under this programme, financial institutions granted more than 8,100 conversions amounting to $200 million of personal unsecured debt.

sections.label: Subsidy for older Singaporeans
sections.summary: Singaporeans aged 40 and above get 90% subsidy and need only pay $161.50, with GST.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: For Singaporeans aged 40 and above, however, they get 90% subsidy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: For them, they need only pay $161.50, with GST.

sections.label: Wage support for disabled persons
sections.summary: The plan provides a higher tier of 50% wage support under JGI to all Persons with Disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In particular, I support the plan to provide a higher tier of wage support of 50% under JGI to all Persons with Disabilities, a point that hon Member Ms Denise Phua made during her Adjournment Motion yesterday.

sections.label: Ex-offender employment statistics
sections.summary: In 2017, 2018 and 2019, the percentages of ex-offenders who found employment within three months were 55%, 56% and 53%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In terms of statistics, the hon Minister for Home Affairs mentioned that over the past years 2017, 2018 and 2019, the percentage of ex-offenders who found employment within three months are 55%, 56% and 53%.

sections.label: Operator pay and shifts
sections.summary: Most operators work 12-hour shifts for $1,000 to $1,400 monthly and may wear cleanroom jump smocks, while unqualified workers can earn $1,200 to $1,400 as cleaners or delivery riders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Most operators' roles will require a 12-hour-shift and the average monthly pay is between $1,000 and $1,400 and may require workers to wear the cleanroom jump smocks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Now if you do not have any qualification, you can easily make $1,200 to $1,400 or even more as a cleaner or a food delivery rider.

sections.label: Manufacturing industry and foreign workers
sections.summary: Manufacturing contributes about 20% to GDP, averages $100 billion in value, and foreign workers hold about 60% of its jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The manufacturing industry contributes approximately 20% to our GDP and it averages $100 billion in value.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Foreign workers take up about 60% of the jobs in this sector.

sections.label: Travel bubble and fiscal measures
sections.summary: A Hong Kong-Singapore travel bubble was announced, and the speaker covers Singapore's fiscal position, SkillsFuture 2.0, and an enhanced COVID-19 Support Grant funded by re-allocating monies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Significantly, we announced the Hong Kong and Singapore travel bubble today which, hopefully, represents a pathfinder to revive our air travel.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: With the honour of speaking last, I would like to cover Singapore’s fiscal position, SkillsFuture 2.0 to make training efforts impactful and the need for an enhanced version of COVID-19 Support Grant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am comforted that the additional measures announced by the Deputy Prime Minister do not require any further draw on our reserves and will be funded by re-allocating monies.

sections.label: GST hike and online tax leakage
sections.summary: GST hike assumptions must be reviewed for COVID-19's impact, and e-commerce growth makes arresting tax leakage in cross-border online transactions urgent to level the playing field for retailers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The assumptions behind the GST hike must be reviewed to take into account the impact of COVID-19 on people and businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: COVID-19 has also led to an accelerated growth of e-commerce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: It has, therefore, become ever more urgent for Singapore to arrest tax leakage in cross-border online transactions and level the playing field for our retailers.

sections.label: Review COVID-19 Support Grant eligibility
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Deputy Prime Minister to review the COVID-19 Support Grant so workers voluntarily leaving poor-prospect sectors qualify, removing the involuntary unemployment requirement for selected sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I would like, nevertheless, to repeat my call that well-intended assistance to companies that may not have a viable future in the post-COVID-19 world may hinder restructuring efforts and slow down re-allocation of labour and resources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: So, I would like to call on the Deputy Prime Minister to review the COVID-19 Support Grant (CSG) to allow workers who voluntarily leave companies in sectors with poor prospects to also qualify for CSG.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Remove the involuntary unemployment requirement from CSG for workers in selected sectors and set our people free to pursue more promising careers.

sections.label: Extending COVID-19 support schemes
sections.summary: As COVID-19's impact is likely protracted and uncertain, support levels under various schemes need review and extension beyond the period in the Deputy Prime Minister's Ministerial Statement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: With the impact of COVID-19 likely to be protracted and uncertain, the support level provided under various support schemes will also need to be reviewed and extended beyond the period currently provided by the Deputy Prime Minister in his Ministerial Statement.

sections.label: Workfare Income Supplement review urged
sections.summary: Speaker hopes the Government will review the Workfare Income Supplement to top up income for low-wage workers affected by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: With many residents experiencing income reduction, I hope the Government will also review the very strong policy lever they have, the Workfare Income Supplement as a possible means to top-up the income for low-wage workers whose pay has been impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: Third quarter GDP contraction
sections.summary: GDP picked up in the third quarter but still contracted by 7% compared to the same quarter last year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: GDP in the third quarter of this year picked up after the sharp contraction in the previous quarter.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: However, compared to the same quarter last year, GDP still contracted by 7%.

sections.label: Support packages and GDP impact
sections.summary: About $100 billion, or 20% of GDP, was committed over five support packages, expected to avert a 5.6% real GDP loss and save 155,000 jobs yearly.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Together with other schemes, we have committed about $100 billion, or 20% of our GDP, over five support packages.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As I mentioned in my Ministerial Statement last week, our measures are expected to avert a 5.6% loss in real GDP this year and save an average of 155,000 jobs each year in 2020 and 2021.

sections.label: Shift to creating jobs
sections.summary: The focus must shift from job retention to creating jobs, prompting the tapering of the JSS and introduction of the Jobs Growth Incentive.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To do so, we must shift from a focus on job retention to a greater emphasis on creating jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This was why I announced the tapering of the JSS and introduced the Jobs Growth Incentive, or JGI.

sections.label: National Jobs Council opportunities
sections.summary: The National Jobs Council curated 117,500 opportunities as of end-August.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The National Jobs Council has curated 117,500 opportunities as of end-August.

sections.label: Training and job placements
sections.summary: From July to August, over 9,000 individuals were placed into training or job opportunities, bringing total placements to over 33,000.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: From July to August, more than 9,000 individuals were placed into training or job opportunities, bringing the total number of placements to over 33,000.

sections.label: JGI funding for older hires
sections.summary: Under the JGI, eligible companies receive Government funding of up to 50% of the salary of each new local hire aged 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: With the JGI, eligible companies will also receive higher Government funding, at up to 50% of the salary of each new local hire aged 40 and above.

sections.label: Three payouts received
sections.summary: By the end of this month, over 195,000 of them would have received three payouts totalling $9,000.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: By the end of this month, over 195,000 of them would have received three payouts, amounting to $9,000.

sections.label: CSG extension and job search
sections.summary: The CSG was extended to 31 December 2020, with flexibility for appeals and a requirement for applicants to job search or train.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For individuals with extenuating circumstances, we exercise flexibility when we consider their appeals.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have also extended the CSG till 31 December 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As suggested by Mr Leon Perera, in our recent extension of CSG, we have required applicants to actively participate in job search or attend training.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Given the continuing impact of COVID-19 on jobs, we are studying how best to support our workers in this crisis, and how to link support to job search and reskilling, so as to better protect the welfare of our workers.

sections.label: Productivity growth 2016 to 2019
sections.summary: From 2016 to 2019, real value added per actual hour worked rose 2.4% per year, up from 2.2% in the preceding three years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For instance, between 2016 to 2019, overall productivity of our economy measured by real value added per actual hour worked rose by 2.4% per year – an improvement over the 2.2% per annum growth in the preceding three years.

sections.label: Schemes supporting firms
sections.summary: Firms are supported by schemes including the Market Readiness Assistance Grant, Enterprise Development Grant and Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To support our firms, we have a range of schemes including, amongst others, the Market Readiness Assistance Grant, the Enterprise Development Grant, and the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation.

sections.label: ITM clusters and Open Innovation Platform
sections.summary: The 23 ITMs are clustered into six clusters, and firms are urged to use IMDA's Open Innovation Platform to crowdsource solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The 23 ITMs are now clustered into six clusters and we are seeking to look at the synergy within clusters and across clusters, as well as the impact that digitalisation has across all clusters.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: So, I urge our firms to tap on platforms like the Open Innovation Platform launched by IMDA.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: It allows companies to crowdsource innovative solutions from over 9000 companies for their challenges.

sections.label: Old-age support ratio
sections.summary: The old-age support ratio, working-age adults to seniors aged 65 and above, is currently 4.3 to 1.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our current old-age support ratio, defined as the number of working-age adults compared to the number of seniors aged 65 and above, is 4.3 to 1; this is the current number.

sections.label: Household transfers support
sections.summary: This year $5.9 billion in household transfers benefited over 2.8 million residents, averaging $1,500 per citizen household member.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Indeed, we have moved decisively to support households with an unprecedented $5.9 billion of household transfers this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Over 2.8 million Singapore residents have benefited from some combination of our Care and Support Package, Solidarity Payment and Solidarity Utilities Credits.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: On average, citizen households received $1,500 of support for each household member, equivalent to about half a month of their income.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For households in the bottom 50% based on per capita household income, the support received was equivalent to an average of two months of their income.

sections.label: Digital Ambassadors and mental wellness
sections.summary: 1,000 Digital Ambassadors were deployed since June, over 28,000 seniors trained by end-September, and a COVID-19 Mental Wellness Taskforce was set up.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Since June, we have deployed 1,000 Digital Ambassadors, to rally the community and volunteers to support our seniors, hawkers and heartland enterprises to acquire digital skills.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I am glad that as of end-September, more than 28,000 seniors have participated in at least one training programme.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Ensuring access to mental health care is a major priority and requires our collective effort.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have set up a COVID-19 Mental Wellness Taskforce to study ways to strengthen our community (mental) health services, to support new vulnerable groups that may emerge due to the pandemic.

sections.label: Donations platforms collections
sections.summary: Community Chest, Sayang Sayang Fund and Giving.sg received $100 million in donations from January to August this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Key donations platforms such as Community Chest, the Sayang Sayang Fund, and Giving.sg received a total of $100 million in donations from January to August this year.

sections.label: GST rate in 2021
sections.summary: In February this year, it was announced that the GST rate will remain at 7% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In February this year, I announced that the GST rate will remain at 7% in 2021.

sections.label: GST collections and Assurance Package
sections.summary: GST collections are projected down 14%, and a $6 billion Assurance Package will cushion the eventual GST rate increase for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Indeed, GST collections this year are projected to be down by 14% from what we had estimated before the start of the year, mainly due to the travel disruptions and the impact of the circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: However, let me assure Ms Foo that we remain committed to helping our people manage the impact of the GST rate increase.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have already set aside a $6 billion Assurance Package for GST to cushion the increase for Singaporeans when the GST rate is eventually raised.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For most households, this will offset at least five years' worth of additional GST expenses incurred and for those living in 1- to 3- room HDB flats, equivalent to about 10 years' worth of additional GST expenses.

sections.label: Repaying past reserves draw
sections.summary: There is no legal obligation to return past reserves drawn, only a moral duty, and the timeline for rebuilding surpluses is uncertain.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To be clear, under our Constitution, there is no legal obligation for the Government to put back the amount drawn from our past reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Rather, it is about having the moral obligation and sense of duty to current and future generations and the recognition that we are stewards of our reserves which have not come by easily.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: So, it is not possible for me to be definitive on how long it will take for us to build up sufficient surpluses to make up the $52 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The scars it will have on our economy and the global economy are still unknown.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: But I can say that it will not be two years, and I certainly hope it will not take us 50 years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: How long it will take also depend on the choices we make as a country and Government – whether we continue to manage our resources prudently.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We remain committed to running a broadly balanced Budget over each term of Government and will assess the viability of returning the amount drawn, depending on our fiscal position.

sections.label: Citizen letter on reserves
sections.summary: A citizen on medical leave wrote that Singapore cannot afford instability and would be gone if reserves are used up.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Three days ago, one Mr Sim, who was on medical leave wrote to us.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: He was very concerned about the public discussions that we are having, particularly on the use of reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: He said, "Singapore could not afford instability, not like big countries.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Once our reserves are used up, Singapore is gone.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We do not have natural resources to fall back on." So, Mr Speaker, Sir, I thank all Members for your comments and I leave you with this sobering thought from one of our citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Pursuant to Standing Order No 44 (2), the Motion to consider the Ministerial Statement on the Overview of Government's Strategy to Emerge Stronger from the COVID-19 Pandemic lapses at the conclusion of debate.

sections.label: MAS estimates on Budgets
sections.summary: MAS estimates the combined Budgets prevent further GDP contraction and offset unemployment, saving about 155,000 jobs over two years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: MAS estimates that the combined Budgets will prevent the economy from contracting by a further 5.6% of GDP in 2020 and 4.8% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our economic support measures will also offset some of the rise in resident unemployment rate by about 1.7 percentage points this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This could mean about 155,000 jobs saved over these two years, although we will still see job losses overall.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: More than half of the jobs saved are due to the Jobs Support Scheme or JSS alone.

sections.label: Extending ETSP support
sections.summary: The Enhanced Training Support Package is extended six months to 30 June 2021, expanded to Marine and Offshore, with lower absentee payroll rates from January 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In addition, we will extend the Enhanced Training Support Package, or ETSP, which I enhanced in the Resilience Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will extend the ETSP for another six months, until 30 June 2021, to provide enhanced course fee subsidies for firms in our hardest-hit sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will extend the ETSP to the Marine and Offshore sector from today, on top of the existing sectors, such as Air Transport, Retail, and Tourism.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In recognition of the gradually recovering economic situation, we will also be lowering the absentee payroll rates to 80% from January 2021, capped at $7.50 per hour.

sections.label: Wage support for disabilities
sections.summary: Persons with Disabilities will receive the higher tier of 50% wage support under the JGI.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As persons with disabilities may face greater challenges in finding jobs, I will provide the higher tier of wage support of 50% under the JGI to all Persons with Disabilities.

sections.label: SGUnited opportunities curated
sections.summary: The Council has curated 117,500 opportunities under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package as of end-August.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Council has curated 117,500 opportunities under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package as of end-August.

sections.label: Matching workers to opportunities
sections.summary: SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centres in every HDB town and Career Ambassadors help workers know of and be matched to opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The key task is now to make sure that workers know of and are successfully matched to these opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have set up SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centres in every HDB town and have Career Ambassadors to reach out to residents.

sections.label: COVID-19 Support Grant extension
sections.summary: MSF extended the COVID-19 Support Grant for those who lost jobs, with applications open until the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To help those who have lost their jobs, MSF has recently extended the COVID-19 Support Grant, and applications are open until the end of the year.

sections.label: One-off support for newborns
sections.summary: To help with expenses amid income uncertainty, a one-off additional support for newborns will be introduced.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is fully understandable, especially when they face uncertainty with their income.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Hence, to help with expenses during this period, we will introduce a one-off additional support for newborns.

sections.label: Pre-COVID unemployment and income figures
sections.summary: Before COVID-19, resident unemployment was 3.2% at end-2019, productivity rose 2.4% yearly, and real median income grew 3.7% yearly.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Before COVID-19, our resident unemployment rate was low at 3.2% as at end-2019.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Between 2016 and 2019, overall productivity, measured by real value added per actual hour worked, rose by a creditable 2.4% per year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Overall, real median income for Singaporeans grew by 3.7% per year in the last three years, up from 3.2% in the preceding three years.

sections.label: Fall in passenger traffic
sections.summary: In August, passenger traffic fell over 98% from last year, with daily volume about 3,000 versus 190,000 previously.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Compared with last year, passenger traffic has fallen by more than 98% in August, with daily passenger volume of about 3,000, down sharply from 190,000 previously.

sections.label: Tuas Port and RCEP
sections.summary: Tuas Port's first berths are on track for 2021, and the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership is slated for signing this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The first few berths of Tuas Port are on track to be operational by 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership is slated to be signed this year, connecting a trade region of 15 countries accounting for about 30% of the global population and GDP.

sections.label: Supply chain digitalisation agreements
sections.summary: The Alliance on Supply Chain Digitalisation is exploring options and gathering key supply chain players, and Digital Economy Agreements were concluded with Australia, Chile and New Zealand, with talks ongoing with South Korea.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Within Singapore, the Alliance on Supply Chain Digitalisation is exploring options and bringing together key players across the supply chain in this venture.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have also concluded Digital Economy Agreements with Australia, Chile and New Zealand, and have ongoing talks with South Korea.

sections.label: Enterprise productivity and capability projects
sections.summary: Since January this year, enterprises have started over 27,000 projects to improve productivity and build new capabilities through the Productivity Solutions Grant and Enterprise Development Grant schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Since January this year, enterprises have embarked on over 27,000 projects to improve their productivity and build new capabilities through the Productivity Solutions Grant and the Enterprise Development Grant schemes.

sections.label: Funding for worker employment and training
sections.summary: About $3 billion is set aside this year for the SGUnited Jobs and Skills package, on top of close to $5 billion over three years for longer term structural measures.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We want to do so for every worker at every age.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This year, we have set aside about $3 billion for the SGUnited Jobs and Skills package to provide immediate employment and training support for our workers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is on top of the close to $5 billion set aside over three years for our longer term structural measures, to support workers of all ages to upskill and access new job opportunities.

sections.label: PCP employment and wage outcomes
sections.summary: About nine in 10 PCP employees remained employed 24 months after placement, and about seven in 10 saw a wage increase after starting new jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For example, about nine in 10 of PCP employees remained in employment 24 months after being placed, and about seven in 10 saw a wage increase after starting their new jobs.

sections.label: Foreign workforce policies and capabilities
sections.summary: Building on complementary strengths can build cutting-edge capabilities in the workforce and firms and plug into global networks, with foreign workforce policies such as Employment Pass and S Pass rules updated carefully.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: By building on complementary strengths, we can build cutting-edge capabilities in our workforce and our firms and plug into global networks.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will continue to update our foreign workforce policies carefully, such as our Employment Pass and S Pass rules, to achieve this synergy.

sections.label: Workfare Skills Support for lower income workers
sections.summary: Lower income workers get additional skills upgrading support via the Workfare Skills Support scheme, implemented in July 2020 to support acquisition of skills and qualifications more likely to lead to higher wages.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our lower income workers also get additional support for skills upgrading via the Workfare Skills Support scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This has been implemented in July 2020 to better support acquisition of skills and qualifications that are more likely to lead to higher wages.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Mark and PWM expansion
sections.summary: Companies paying progressive wages get a PWM Mark, foreign workforce growth will slow, and more sectors may adopt the PWM framework.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Companies that voluntarily pay progressive wages and provide advancement pathways for lower income workers will also be recognised with a PWM Mark.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: And in time, we will slow down the future growth of the foreign workforce in these sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We may still be battling the downturn, but will be actively looking to identify the next few sectors where we can use the four-in-one PWM framework to redesign jobs and raise skills levels, and expand PWM to benefit more groups of lower wage workers as soon as conditions allow.

sections.label: Job matching for displaced workers
sections.summary: Job openings placed at touchpoints like Social Services Offices and MyCareersFuture can facilitate matches, and Low Yen Ling will study help for displaced mature professionals.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: By putting these job openings together, and placing them at potential touchpoints like Social Services Offices, Community Centres, MyCareersFuture portal, and SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centres, we can facilitate job matches for these workers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I have asked Minister of State Low Yen Ling, who is also Chairperson of the Mayors' Committee, to look into how we can better help our displaced mature professionals, and how we can make better use of micro-jobs to bring job opportunities closer to the heartlands.

sections.label: Funding COVID-19 support measures
sections.summary: Continued COVID-19 support costs a further $8 billion this financial year, funded by reallocating monies from areas with reduced spending.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As I announced in my August's Ministerial Statement, the continued support for our fight against COVID-19 will cost a further $8 billion this financial year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The additional measures I have spoken on today remain within this and earlier voted sums.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will fund the additional expenditure by reallocating monies from other areas with reduced spending, such as development projects that have been delayed due to COVID-19.

sections.label: Draw on Past Reserves
sections.summary: The revised estimates reflect a $1.5 billion draw on Past Reserves from measures like the Foreign Worker Levy waiver, approved in-principle by the President.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The revised estimates will reflect a $1.5 billion draw on Past Reserves resulting from these measures, such as the Foreign Worker Levy waiver, for which the President had given in-principle approval.

sections.label: Total support for people and businesses
sections.summary: Close to $100 billion in total is being dedicated to support people and businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In total, we are dedicating close to $100 billion to support our people and businesses.

sections.label: Fall in revenue collections
sections.summary: Revenue collections are expected to fall across all categories, with GST collections down 14% compared to start-of-year estimates.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Revenue collections are expected to fall across all categories of revenue.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For example, compared to the estimates at the start of the year, we expect GST collections to be down by 14%.

sections.label: Fiscal resources for crisis
sections.summary: Close to $100 billion is dedicated to support people and businesses through this difficult period.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: What is within our control is how we use our fiscal resources well to respond to this crisis and to prepare for the future.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have dedicated close to $100 billion to support our people and businesses through this difficult period.

sections.label: Temporary Bridging Loan Programme extension
sections.summary: The Temporary Bridging Loan Programme is extended until September 2021 at reduced levels for businesses facing liquidity problems.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I understand that many businesses are still facing liquidity problems.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will extend the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme until September 2021, at reduced levels.

sections.label: Prudence in planning finances
sections.summary: The guiding principle is prudence, not austerity, with continued investment in families, healthcare and infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Despite this, our guiding principle is prudence, not austerity, when planning our finances.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will continue to invest resources in families, healthcare and infrastructure to enhance the quality of life of our people.

sections.label: Support, reopening and economic strategy
sections.summary: Commitment to support workers and businesses, steps to re-open safely, and a refreshed economic strategy for a post-COVID-19 world.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I have shared with this House and our people a stocktake of where we are, and where we are headed.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I give you our commitment that we will continue to support our workers and businesses in this difficult time.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have worked out the steps to further re-open safely in the coming months.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have refreshed our economic strategy for a post-COVID-19 world, to remake Singapore as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation, and enterprise, achieve inclusive growth and build resilience and sustainability, so as to achieve better lives and opportunities for our people.
